recap: On the heels of a season in which he won his first Most Valu- able Player award and helped lead Oklahoma City to its first NBA cham- pionship, Gilgeous-Alexander had another outstanding campaign. Shoot- ing a career-high 55.3 percent from the field, the Thunder star wasn’t far off from his first 50/40/90 season and helped lead Oklahoma City to the league’s best record. One of the most productive players in fantasy bas- ketball regardless of format, Gilgeous-Alexander won NBA MVP honors for a second consecutive season.
changed: For SGA specifically, nothing has changed, as he remains the cornerstone in Oklahoma City. However, some members of the supporting cast have changed, with Luguentz Dort (Atlanta), Isaiah Joe (Detroit) and Aaron Wiggins (Atlanta) all being traded this offseason.
outlook: While most of the conversation regarding Pick 1.1 in fantasy drafts has focused on San Antonio’s Victor Wembanyama and Denver’s Ni- kola Jokić, Gilgeous-Alexander is far from a “consolation prize.” He should remain a high draft pick, slotting in right after Wemby and “The Joker.” It would be surprising if Gilgeous-Alexander does not produce another elite fantasy season while seeking to become the first player to win three con- secutive MVP awards since Larry Bird (1984-86).

recap: Dončić’s first full season with the Lakers was one in which he was able to truly cement his status as the franchise’s cornerstone. While he did miss the final five games of the regular season and the entirety of the Lakers’ postseason run with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain, the point guard received a waiver that made him eligible for end-of-season honors. A first-team All-NBA selection, Dončić led the league in scoring, field goals and three-point field goals per game.
changed: The Lakers’ “big three” is no more, as LeBron James agreed to a two-year deal with the 76ers in free agency. Also of note was the team’s acquisition of Walker Kessler, who should be a better fit alongside Dončić than Deandre Ayton was.
outlook: No LeBron in the picture and the addition of Kessler, a legiti- mate lob threat, may give Dončić’s assist production a boost after he aver- aged 8.3 helpers per game in 2025-26. While some managers in nine-cat leagues may have an issue with the turnover tally, Luka does enough in other areas to compensate for that issue. He’ll be a top five pick in fantasy drafts, and provided he remains relatively healthy, Dončić should not have much trouble meeting those expectations.

recap: While his scoring output decreased in comparison to 2024- 25, Cunningham’s assists and steals increased last season. He earned a second consecutive All-Star Game appearance and led the Pistons to the best record in the East, earning first-team All-NBA honors and finishing fifth in MVP voting. A top 20 player in nine-cat formats, Cunningham of- fered top 10 value to managers in eight-cat formats and those willing to punt turnovers. The end to his season may have been a disappointment, with the Pistons being eliminated in the second round of the playoffs, but Cunningham is becoming the player Detroit hoped he would be when they selected him first overall in the 2021 draft.
changed: Cunningham’s status as Detroit’s cornerstone is unchanged, but some of the options around him have. Tobias Harris moved to San Antonio in free agency, with the Pistons signing John Collins to fill that void. Also, Isaiah Joe was added via trade in hopes of surrounding the star point guard with more shooting.
outlook: Even with the turnover concerns, Cunningham should not fall out of the first ten picks in fantasy drafts, regardless of league format. With Collins and Joe in the fold, the hope is that he can increase the as- sists even more after averaging a career-high 9.9 per game last season. As long as he can remain reasonably healthy, having appeared in at least 62 games each of the last three seasons, Cunningham will be immensely valuable to fantasy managers.

recap: An All-Star each of the last four seasons, Edwards missed out on All-NBA honors because he did not hit the 65-game minimum. Howev- er, he was highly productive when available, averaging a career-high 28.8 points per game. His rebounds and assists fell compared to the 2024-25 averages, but Edwards was more efficient as a scorer and playmaker. De- spite a lingering knee injury, Ant-Man helped lead the Timberwolves to the second round of the playoffs, where they were eliminated by the eventual Western Conference champion Spurs.
changed: While Edwards’ role remains the same, some of the options around him have changed. Minnesota acquired LaMelo Ball from the Hornets in a multi-team deal that sent Julius Randle to Brooklyn and Naz Reid to Charlotte. Jonathan Kuminga was signed as a free agent, and Donte DiVincenzo will miss a significant portion of next season (if not all of it) as he recovers from a ruptured Achilles tendon.
outlook: Ball’s addition should make the Timberwolves more explo- sive offensively, but it may also force the team to ask more of Edwards defensively. If that leads to increased “stocks” production from Ant-Man, fantasy managers won’t complain, especially if his efficiency continues to improve. After providing second-round value in fantasy basketball last season, Edwards is more than capable of jumping into the first round, which is when he should be selected in most drafts.

recap: Due to the devastating Achilles tendon rupture he suffered during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, Haliburton did not play at all last season. He’s averaged at least nine assists per game in each of his three full seasons with the Pacers, offering 19.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, 10.1 assists, 1.5 steals and 2.8 blocks in 224 appearances for the franchise.
changed: First and foremost, Haliburton is healthy and has a clean bill of health going into training camp. Among the Pacers who were not on the team when he last played are center Ivica Zubac and reserve wing Kelly Oubre Jr., with the former offering more rebounding production than Myles Turner did.
outlook: Given the time missed, fantasy managers will need to keep their expectations for Haliburton in check, at least early in the season. However, he has shown first-round fantasy potential when healthy, and managers should expect to see that version of Haliburton at some point. Haliburton won’t be selected that early because of the Achilles injury, making him a potential steal in drafts.

recap: Limited to 52 games the season prior due to injury, Maxey appeared in 70 games last season. Earning his second All-Star Game invitation, the 76ers guard finished with career-high averages in points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks while playing a league-high 38.0 min- utes per game. While Maxey was a third-team All-NBA selection, he was far from his best in the playoffs due to a finger injury on his right hand. His struggles were one reason the 76ers were swept by the Knicks in the second round.
changed: The 76ers improved their starting lineup immense- ly this summer, signing LeBron James in free agency and acquiring Jaylen Brown from the Celtics in exchange for Paul George. The stronger starting five should take some of the weight off Maxey’s shoulders, especially with the lingering concerns regarding Joel Embiid’s availability.
outlook: James’ arrival means that Maxey won’t be asked to initiate of- fense as often as he has been in the past. While the assists may take a hit, there will also be more opportunities for him to attack closeouts. Maxey’s fantasy value may take a slight hit, but he remains worthy of first-round consideration, regardless of league format. Because even with James and Brown in the fold, fantasy managers also have to take Embiid’s availability issues into consideration when evaluating Maxey’s role.

recap: An All-Star in each of his last seven seasons, Mitchell earned second-team All-NBA honors in 2025-26. Compared to the prior season, his points, assists and steals averages all increased as he helped lead the Cavaliers to their first conference finals appearance since 2018. However, Mitchell’s production wasn’t enough to keep Cleveland from getting swept by the eventual NBA champion Knicks.
changed: The “core four” changed last winter, with Cleve- land acquiring James Harden from the Clippers in a package that included Darius Garland. Some of the supporting cast members have moved on, with Max Strus (Clippers), Dennis Schröder (Hornets) and Keon Ellis (Nets) no longer in the picture, but Mitchell’s role is unchanged.
outlook: After the trade deadline, Mitchell averaged 26.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, 5.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game, with his numbers only taking a slight hit following Harden’s arrival. In theory, those two should have even better on-court chemistry, benefiting both produc- tion-wise. Mitchell should not fall beyond the third round in standard 12- team drafts this fall.

recap: The Warriors struggled with injuries throughout last season, and Curry wasn’t exempt. He appeared in just 43 games, with a knee injury that became problematic in late January, sidelining him for just over two months. Curry appeared in four of Golden State’s final games of the regu- lar season, but that was too late for managers in most fantasy leagues. His scoring average increased by just over two points per game compared to 2024-25, jumping to 26.6.
changed: Some of the injuries from last season will carry over into the 2026-27 campaign, as Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody con- tinue to recover from their knee injuries. The Warriors also didn’t make a splash in free agency, signing Georges Niang and Brandon Williams to partially guaranteed deals and using their first-round pick to select Mich- igan forward Yaxel Lendeborg.
outlook: When available, Curry has consistently provided first-round fantasy value, regardless of league format. While some may see the Butler and Moody injuries as a chance for Curry to offer more early, the War- riors also have to consider his age (38) and the “long game.” Using a sec- ond-round pick on the greatest shooter of all-time is reasonable; the first round would be a reach in most leagues.

recap: After appearing in 75 games the season prior, Booker made 64 appearances for the Suns in 2025-26. A sprained right ankle suffered in mid-January factored into the All-Star guard missing seven consecutive games before playing two of Phoenix’s final three games before the break. A strained right hip suffered in the Suns’ first game after the break would sideline Booker for four more games, and after his return, he would not miss another until April 10. During March, which is “prime time” in most fantasy leagues, Booker averaged 28.8 points, 3.7 rebounds, 5.6 assists and 2.4 three-pointers per game (16 games). While his production did not match his ADP (11), Booker finished the season as a top 50 player in eight- cat formats.
changed: Booker remains the Suns’ cornerstone, but the rotation around him has changed. Miles Bridges was acquired from the Hornets in a deal that sent Grayson Allen and Royce O’Neale in the oppo- site direction. Phoenix also signed Luke Kennard in free agency, adding another shooter to the mix.
outlook: Given his importance to the Suns’ rotation, Booker is well-po- sitioned to provide excellent fantasy value. However, managers should not go into drafts expecting a first-round return. While Booker’s scoring aver- age did increase slightly compared to the 2024-25 production, there were dips in rebounds, assists and three-pointers. With Bridges in the fold and the point guard situation more solidified thanks to the re-signing of Collin Gillespie, Booker should not be considered in standard league drafts until the latter stages of the second round.

recap: After appearing in 62 and 69 games in his first two seasons, Thompson only missed three games in 2025-26. He recorded career-high averages in points, assists and steals, with the second category receiving a slight boost due to Fred VanVleet being sidelined by a torn ACL. Thomp- son missed out on All-Defensive Team honors but finished eighth in voting for Defensive Player of the Year. Fantasy-wise, he provided third-round per-game value in nine-cat formats despite offering little as a perimeter shooter.
changed: Thompson’s biggest change was getting paid, agreeing to an extension worth about $208 million over five years that will take effect next season. Whatever doubts there may have been about his status as a cornerstone in Houston were put to rest when Thompson agreed to the deal on September 3.
outlook: While Thompson needs to further improve his perimeter shot to help the Rockets in their quest to win a championship, that is not a concern for fantasy managers. He does enough across the board to offer excellent value despite the poor shooting, but this does limit his ceiling. Using a second-round pick on Thompson is not a reach, and it isn’t as if he needs to turn into Stephen Curry to exceed that.

recap: Young’s 2025-26 season marked the end of an era, as the point guard was traded to the Wizards after seven-plus seasons with the Hawks. He was injured at the time of the deal, having suffered a knee injury in late October. Young appeared in just five games for the Wizards and 15 overall, with a quad injury that shut him down for the rest of the season in mid-March. Young finished the season with career-low averages in points, rebounds, assists and three-pointers.
changed: Young’s future in Washington was cemented, as he agreed to a four-year extension worth close to $213 million. Also, the Wizards selected AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick, which makes him one of the team’s cornerstones alongside Young and center Alex Sarr.
outlook: When healthy, Young is an elite fantasy point guard despite the turnover issues. While last season was the first in which he did not average at least 3.8 turnovers per game, as noted above, “Ice Trae” only appeared in 15 games. Young is a better option for managers in eight-cat formats and points leagues than nine-cat, but good luck getting him out- side of the first two rounds of drafts regardless of format.

recap: Murray enjoyed one of the best and healthiest seasons of his NBA career, making 75 appearances and earning his first All-Star Game nod. He finished the season with career-high averages in points, rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and was close to a 50/40/90 player. Murray was at his best in January, averaging 27.7 points and 8.6 assists per game in 11 appearances.
changed: Murray continues to slot in as Nikola Jokić’s trust- ed sidekick, but the Nuggets’ depth took a hit with the departure of Peyton Watson. Denver did sign DeMar DeRozan in free agency, and the veteran wing is capable of helping out offensively.
outlook: Murray playing 75 games last season will likely push him up some draft boards, and he’s played at least 65 in three of his last four seasons since missing all of 2021-22 with a torn ACL. However, while some may be willing to grab him in the second round of standard league drafts, the third round would be a safer spot for the Nuggets guard.

recap: For the first time since the 2021-22 campaign, his second in the NBA, Ball managed to surpass 60 regular-season games. The point guard played in 72 games for the Hornets, and while the points average decreased, his assists held steady as Brandon Miller and rookie Kon Knueppel took on more of the scoring workload. Ball may not have earned any end-of-season honors, but the 2025-26 campaign represented a step in the right direction for him.
changed: After six seasons in Charlotte, Ball was sent to Min- nesota as part of a multi-team trade. He’ll join forces with another exciting 25-year-old guard, Anthony Edwards.
outlook: The change of scenery may benefit Ball, as he joins a fran- chise that has experienced recent postseason success and had an un- questioned cornerstone in Edwards. However, fantasy managers will be more interested in whether joining forces with Edwards will make Ball more efficient. He’s shot 41 percent or worse from the field in three of the last four seasons, but 2025-26 was the first season in which Ball averaged less than three turnovers per game since his rookie year. The back end of the second round would be a good area to target LaMelo in standard drafts.

recap: Harden began his 17th NBA season with the Clippers, but it eventually became clear that a change would be necessary. The financial security the point guard was seeking was unlikely to come in Los Angeles, so Harden was traded to Cleveland just before the February deadline. He appeared in 26 regular-season games for the Cavaliers, averaging 20.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 3.1 three-pointers while shooting 46.6 percent from the field and 84.0 percent from the foul line. Helping lead the Cavaliers to their first conference finals appearance since 2018, Harden finished last season as a top 25 player in fantasy basketball.
changed: Harden opted out of the final year of his contract, doing so to give the Cavaliers added flexibility in the front office’s attempt to improve the roster. The Beard eventually agreed to a three-year deal worth about $97 million, locking him into the point guard role alongside Donovan Mitchell.
outlook: At 37 years old, Harden is in the twilight of his NBA career. While he isn’t the prolific scorer that he was during his prime with the Rockets, he remains a productive and valuable point guard option for fantasy managers regardless of league format. The best course of action for managers in standard 12-team leagues would be to begin considering Harden towards the end of the second round, even though he’s capable of offering greater value.

recap: Since arriving in New York in the summer of 2022, Brunson has been the answer at point guard that Knicks fans and the organiza- tion hoped he would be. And that may be a conservative statement. A third-team All-NBA selection each of the last three seasons, Brunson led the Knicks to their first NBA title in 53 years, scoring 45 points in the ti- tle-clinching Game 5 win over the Spurs in San Antonio. His fantasy value may not have aligned with his ADP (21), but Brunson was far from a disap- pointment as he finished the regular season as a top 50 player in nine-cat formats.
changed: Most of the Knicks’ rotation has remained, with Mitchell Robinson (Celtics) being the only departure. Otherwise, every- thing remains the same for Brunson as he enters the first season of his thirties.
outlook: The Knicks made a tweak to their offensive approach during the first round of the playoffs, putting more playmaking responsibilities upon Karl-Anthony Towns’ shoulders. However, Brunson’s production did not take a hit. If anything, sharing the responsibilities benefited the point guard. Given New York’s rotation, using a second-round pick on Brunson may be a slight reach, but not by much. His floor will be safe regardless of league format.

recap: While injuries limited him to a career-low 51 games, Reaves picked a good time to have the most productive statistical season of his NBA career. The Lakers guard posted career-high averages in points and rebounds while shooting 49 percent from the field. Due to the games played, Reaves missed out on postseason honors, but the production was enough to drive up the price as he went into unrestricted free agency.
changed: As expected, Reaves got paid in a major way, agreeing to a four-year deal worth nearly $185 million. There were also some key personnel changes, with LeBron James (76ers), Rui Hachimura (Clippers) and Marcus Smart (Rockets) signing elsewhere in free agen- cy, and Deandre Ayton (Wizards) being traded. Among the new additions were guards Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton.
outlook: With LeBron no longer in the picture, Reaves’ role stands to expand next season. The question is whether that will have a negative im- pact on his efficiency, especially after Reaves averaged a career-high 3.0 turnovers per game last season. However, even with that question, it’s fair to bet on Reaves’ fantasy upside, which should make him a second-round pick in standard leagues.

recap: While injuries limited him to 54 appearances, Giddey’s sec- ond season in Chicago was more productive than his first. The 6-foot-7 guard provided improved numbers in points, rebounds, assists and three-pointers, averaging career highs in all four categories. From late December through the All-Star break, Giddey appeared in just four games as he dealt with a strained left hamstring. He also missed six of Chicago’s final seven games and underwent offseason surgery on his right ankle.
changed: The good news is that Giddey has made signif- icant strides in his recovery from ankle surgery and was cleared in late August to resume playing 5-on-5 without restrictions. Rotation-wise, his role is unchanged, but the Bulls added first-round picks Caleb Wilson and Dailyn Swain via the draft and acquired Nic Claxton from the Nets to ad- dress their need for a starting center.
outlook: With Giddey healthy, plus two newcomers in Wilson and Clax- ton to get the ball to, his assist output could rise. And while questions re- main about his shooting, Giddey has shot a respectable 37.1 percent from three in his two seasons with the Bulls. New head coach Tiago Splitter will rely on the Australian guard to run the show, making it possible for him to take another step forward in his development. Giddey finished last season just outside the top 50 in fantasy value; he’s well-positioned to be more productive in 2026-27.

recap: After spending his first five seasons in Memphis, Bane was traded to Orlando last summer. His first season with the Magic was pro- ductive, as Bane averaged 20 points per game for the third time in four seasons. Despite the rebound, assist and three-point averages taking slight hits compared to his 2024-25 numbers, Bane still provided fourth- round fantasy value in eight- and nine-cat formats. This was also the first season he played in all 82 regular-season games.
changed: The Magic will have a new head coach, with for- mer Spurs lead assistant Sean Sweeney replacing Jamahl Mosley, but Bane’s role should remain the same as one of the better two-way guards in the NBA.
outlook: Bane’s fantasy ceiling in Orlando may be slightly lower than it was in Memphis due to the presence of Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner, but he boasts a reliable floor. The fourth round would be a good place to target him; Bane is unlikely to last past the fifth round in any fantasy draft.

recap: Having suffered a torn ACL in his left knee in March 2025, Ir- ving was not officially ruled out for the entire 2025-26 season until the All-Star break in February.
changed: First and foremost, Irving will be good to go when the Mavericks open training camp in late September. The cast around him has also changed, with reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg now the franchise cornerstone and veterans Anthony Davis (Wizards) and Klay Thompson (Heat) no longer in the fold. Lastly, the Mavericks have a new head coach, with former Michigan head coach Dusty May replacing Jason Kidd.
outlook: Irving is an elite guard when healthy but using an early-round draft pick on him would be a reach, given the time missed. Add in Flagg’s presence and a new head coach, and looking for Irving in the fifth round of drafts would be a good place to start. If he can remain relatively healthy, Kyrie could be one of the steals in fantasy basketball this season. However, he has surpassed 65 regular-season games just once since the 2016-17 campaign.

recap: With Jayson Tatum sidelined to begin the season with a rup- tured Achilles, White was one of the Celtics who appeared well-positioned to benefit as a scorer. However, he had the worst shooting season of his NBA career, failing to make at least 40 percent of his field-goal attempts for the first time. The production across the board was good enough to compensate for that deficiency, with White still offering top 50 fantasy value regardless of format. He’s appeared in at least 73 games in each of the last five seasons, giving fantasy managers nothing to worry about regarding White’s availability.
changed: This summer marked the end of an era in Bos- ton, as the Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers in exchange for Paul George. That shift won’t have much of an impact on White’s place within the rotation, but George’s recent injury history may mean more opportuni- ties for the veteran guard throughout the course of the 2026-27 campaign.
outlook: Even when White shoots the ball poorly, as he did for most of the 2025-26 season, he’s good enough to offer excellent fantasy value, es- pecially in category leagues. A healthy Tatum may boost White’s shooting efficiency, as can the presence of George, considering the newest Celtic’s ability to knock down perimeter shots. While he may be a player who is available on draft boards in the fourth round, White is more than capable of exceeding that expectation.

recap: The left great toe injury that Garland initially suffered during the latter stages of the 2024-25 regular season required offseason sur- gery to address, pushing his 2025-26 debut back to early November. And even then, he wasn’t at full strength, with Garland not appearing in three consecutive games until December. Garland sprained his left great toe in January, an injury that sidelined him until early March, and he was traded to the Clippers during that time off the floor. In 19 games for the Clippers, Garland averaged 19.9 points, 6.4 assists, 1.2 steals and 3.3 three-pointers per game.
changed: The biggest change affecting Garland hasn’t happened yet; the trade that would send Kawhi Leonard to Toronto in ex- change for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft compensation is still on hold. Given what the Clippers lost in the NBA’s investigation into their signing of Kawhi, getting that draft capital (two future firsts) is critical. Garland will continue to run the show, but it’s possible that lottery pick Keaton Wagler siphons some of those opportunities.
outlook: When healthy, Garland can provide reliable middle-round fan- tasy value. However, he’s appeared in fewer than 60 games in two of the last three seasons, which may concern some fantasy managers at draft time. If the Leonard trade goes through, Garland will be worth the risk in the middle rounds of drafts, as there will be more opportunities for him to produce as a scorer.

recap: The fourth overall pick in the 2025 draft, Knueppel’s rookie campaign went better than most anticipated. Missing just one game, the former Duke guard was one of the favorites for Rookie of the Year honors throughout the season, ultimately finishing second to college teammate Cooper Flagg. Knueppel set the rookie record for three-pointers in a sea- son and finished as a sixth-round player in eight- and nine-cat formats.
changed: This summer marked the beginning of a new era in Charlotte, as LaMelo Ball (Timberwolves) and Miles Bridges (Suns) moved on in separate trades. As a result, Knueppel and Brandon Miller will be the focal points as the Hornets look to reach the playoffs for the first time since 2016.
outlook: While the Hornets re-signed Coby White and added Dennis Schröder via trade, it’s expected that Knueppel will have the ball in his hands more than he did as a rookie. Combine that with how well he per- formed last season, and it’s fair to expect an even better campaign from Knueppel. Top 50 value should represent his floor in fantasy basketball; managers may want to consider grabbing Knueppel in the latter stages of the third round.

recap: Herro failed to reach 50 games for the second time in three seasons, with injuries limiting him to 33 appearances in 2025-26. A left ankle injury that would require surgery sidelined him for the first 17 games of the season, and a toe injury suffered in December put him on the bench for another month. Herro played five games before a rib injury sidelined him for another month, and in April he underwent right foot surgery.
changed: After spending seven seasons with the Heat, Herro was one of the players traded to the Bucks this summer as part of the deal that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to Miami. Going into the final season of his current contract, Herro joins a team that is rebuilding after bidding farewell to arguably the best player in franchise history.
outlook: With Giannis no longer in the fold, Herro will have every op- portunity to show that he’s a player the Bucks can build around for the future. And even if the front office decides to prioritize cap space, an excellent 2026-27 season would go a long way toward getting Herro the payday he desires. Fantasy-wise, he’s capable of providing top 50 value regardless of league format. However, the Bucks’ perimeter rotation is a bit crowded with holdovers Ryan Rollins, Kevin Porter Jr. and Gary Trent Jr., and lottery pick Brayden Burries. Playing time won’t be an issue for Herro, but the overall rotation lowers his ceiling.

recap: Having suffered a ruptured Achilles tendon during a game on January 31, 2025, Murray did not make his first appearance of the 2025-26 season until the Pelicans’ third game out of the All-Star break. The veteran guard appeared in 14 games before being shut down for the final five of the regular season, starting each with then-rookie big Derik Queen being bumped to the bench. Murray offered good fantasy value when available, ranking in the top 100 in eight- and nine-cat formats.
changed: The Pelicans have a new head coach, with Jamahl Mosley taking the reins after doing a solid job of rebuilding the Orlando Magic. Murray’s role should remain the same as it was when healthy last season, but it’s possible that he plays less as the Pelicans look to get Jer- emiah Fears more reps at point guard.
outlook: The current rotation in New Orleans complicates matters, as it mixes veterans still capable of producing with two rookies in Queen and Fears who are also worthy of significant playing time. With Murray go- ing into the final guaranteed season of his contract, a good start to the season could result in his name being mentioned in trade rumors as the February deadline approaches. When healthy, he’s certainly capable of providing reliable middle-round value in standard leagues, if not better. That is where fantasy managers should target Murray in drafts.

recap: Playing his first full season with the Spurs after being acquired from the Kings in February 2025, Fox started all 72 regular-season games that he appeared in. Compared to his production in 17 games for the Spurs in 2024-25, Fox experienced slight decreases in points, rebounds, assists and steals. However, he shot better from the field and beyond the arc, like- ly benefiting from the increased availability of Spurs star Victor Wemban- yama. While Fox was a key contributor for a team that won the Western Conference, his season ended on a sour note due to struggles in the NBA Finals. But that wasn’t an issue for fantasy managers, as the veteran point guard’s value hovered around the top 75 all season long.
changed: The combination of Fox’s struggles against the Knicks and Dylan Harper’s stellar rookie campaign may lead to the latter getting more minutes in 2026-27. It’s possible that Fox loses out on some playing time, but not to the point where serious damage would be done to his fantasy value. Luka Doncic Photo by William Liang-Imagn Images
outlook: The most significant issue for Fox in fantasy basketball, es- pecially in category leagues, has been the foul line. After making nearly 83 percent of his attempts in 2024-25, his percentage dropped to 76.0 in 2025-26, only slightly higher than his career number (74.7). Even with the possibility of Harper playing more, fantasy managers should not be overly concerned with what that may mean for Fox. Selecting him within the first 75 picks in category leagues is a wise course of action, as Fox has offered that level of value in most seasons.

recap: Going into his third season, George had work to do if he was to convince the Jazz front office that he should be the starting point guard moving forward. Well, he answered the bell, and had he played in enough games, he may have been considered for Most Improved Player honors. George finished the season with career-high averages in points, assists and steals. Injuries limited George to 54 games, his last being on March 11, so he wasn’t much help to fantasy managers during the play- off weeks. While on the court, George was a top 50 player in category leagues.
changed: George is healthy, as are Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Walker Kessler (Lakers) moved on via sign-and-trade, which likely means that Jusuf Nurkić will be the starting center. After years of rebuilding, the Jazz are expected to do all they can to compete for a postseason spot, especially with the NBA changing its draft lottery rules.
outlook: George being Utah’s unquestioned starting point guard makes him a far more reliable option in fantasy drafts than he was last fall. While Markkanen and Jackson being on the floor likely means less scoring for George, his assist output should benefit. Targeting George just outside the first 50 picks would be a wise approach to take in standard drafts.

recap: The third overall pick in the 2025 draft, Edgecombe lived up to the preseason hype for the 76ers. Appearing in 75 games, the athletic guard formed a reliable partnership with Tyrese Maxey and offered top 75 fantasy value. Edgecombe, whose productivity was three rounds better than his ADP, finished third in Rookie of the Year voting behind Dallas’ Coo- per Flagg and Charlotte’s Kon Knueppel.
changed: The 76ers made two major moves this offseason that are likely to impact Edgecombe’s role. The first was ot acquire Jaylen Brown from the Celtics, with Paul George headed in the opposite direction. The second was the signing of LeBron James to a two-year contract.
outlook: While Edgecombe’s fantasy value should not drop significant- ly, it can be argued that the additions of Brown and James will lower his ceiling. That said, fantasy managers should also consider the availability questions surrounding center Joel Embiid, who has not played 40 games in any of the last three seasons. Edgecombe is a worthwhile middle-round pick in standard leagues, with the end of the fifth round being a good place to begin targeting him.

recap: Morant appeared in 12 of the Grizzlies’ first 14 games before a right ankle injury sidelined him for nearly a month. Unfortunately, there would be another extended absence for him in January before an elbow injury forced him to the sideline for the rest of the season. Morant, who has not exceeded 65 games since his rookie season, appeared in 79 games over his final three seasons in Memphis, thanks to extended absences due to injuries and a few suspensions. It became clear his time with the Grizzlies was coming to an end, but the team couldn’t pull off a deal during the season.
changed: The Grizzlies found a trade partner in the offsea- son, sending Morant to the Trail Blazers for Jerami Grant, Kris Murray and a trade exception. Given the highs that Morant experienced in Memphis, that was a shocking return, but it also indicated how far he’s fallen in recent years.
outlook: When available, Morant can offer excellent fantasy value, especially for managers willing to ignore the turnover issues. However, availability has long been a concern, and Portland’s backcourt situation won’t be easy to navigate. Damian Lillard is returning from a ruptured Achilles tendon, while Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson also remain on the roster. How first-year head coach Micah Nori will juggle the minutes at guard remains to be seen, especially with Holiday being the lone “plus” defender. Obviously, Morant should be selected in drafts, but fantasy man- agers need to keep their expectations in check, even if he gets off to a hot start.

recap: White began the season on the bench, as a strained calf lim- ited him when the Bulls opened training camp. And just as he was pre- paring for a return, the guard suffered a Grade 2 ankle sprain, pushing his season debut back to mid-November. And the timing could not have been worse for White, who was in a contract year. Sure enough, he was traded to the Hornets at the February deadline, with another calf strain sidelin- ing him until after the All-Star break, which forced the Bulls to amend the deal (since the injury was not disclosed to the Hornets). In 21 games for Charlotte, White averaged 15.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.0 three-pointers.
changed: Two significant changes impacting White this summer. He and the Hornets agreed to a three-year, $74 million deal, and LaMelo Ball was traded to the Timberwolves. While Charlotte added veter- an guard Dennis Schröder in a separate transaction, White is expected to start the season as the starting point guard.
outlook: Being a starter raises White’s fantasy ceiling, but he won’t be the only player initiating offense for the Hornets. Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller should also have more opportunities to do so with Ball no longer in the picture, in addition to the aforementioned Schröder. Due to his limited defen- sive production, White has usually been a better option for category league managers punting those categories and those competing in points leagues. That could change this season, but White remains a player who should be selected outside the first 75 picks in standard leagues.

recap: After supplying depth off the bench in his first full season with the Bucks, injuries, most specifically to Kevin Porter Jr., opened the door for Rollins to take on a more prominent role. A starter in 67 of the 74 games he played, the 6-foot-3 guard recorded career-high averages in points, re- bounds, assists, steals and three-pointers while playing 32.1 minutes per contest. While Rollins was not a finalist for Most Improved Player honors, there’s no doubt that he was a far more productive player than at any point in his first three seasons.
changed: First and foremost, the Bucks have a new head coach, with Taylor Jenkins replacing Doc Rivers. Another significant change was the end of the Giannis Antetokounmpo era, with his trade to the Heat netting the Bucks a haul that included guards Tyler Herro and Kasparas Jakučionis. Include Gary Trent Jr.’s new contract and the arrival of lottery pick Brayden Burries, and there’s more competition for Rollins to navigate this season.
outlook: Rollins was one of the biggest surprises in fantasy basketball last season, providing top 50 value. However, the Bucks’ perimeter rota- tion has more options than it did in 2025-26, and he’ll be playing for a new head coach. In theory, the development of players like Rollins and Burries should be paramount, but that isn’t guaranteed to be the case. It can be argued that Rollins should be a top 75 pick in standard league drafts, but he’ll be a safer option just outside of that threshold.

recap: After injuries limited him to 33 appearances in his first full season with the Raptors, Quickley remained relatively healthy last season, playing in 70 games. A starter in each, he was close to a top 50 player in category leagues and a top 75 player in points leagues. There was not a huge difference in Quickley’s 2025-26 numbers compared to the season prior, but he did average a career-high 1.3 steals per game.
changed: The one change that stands to impact Quickley and the Raptors most still hadn’t happened at the time of publishing: the trade that would send Kawhi Leonard back to Toronto for Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick hadn’t been finalized. The deal was paused due to the NBA’s investigation into Leonard’s contract with the Clippers. Now that the investigation has concluded, the expectation is that the trade will eventu- ally go through.
outlook: While Quickley has shown himself capable of approaching top 50 fantasy value in Toronto, there seems to be some hesitation on the part of fantasy managers to select him that early in drafts. While Leon- ard’s expected return could cut into IQ’s scoring opportunities, his assists may benefit. Also, adding a defender of Leonard’s caliber could benefit the other Raptors. Even with the availability concerns, Quickley is a safe bet to offer top 75 value, even if he may last longer than that on standard league draft boards.

recap: After winning Rookie of the Year in 2025, Castle recorded improved averages in points, rebounds, assists and steals. The former UConn standout started 67 of the 68 games he appeared in, helping lead the Spurs to the second-best record in the NBA and an NBA Finals ap- pearance. However, there was a significant gap in his eight- and nine- cat fantasy values, with turnovers (3.2 per game) being the issue. While a top 100 player in eight-cat, Castle was ranked outside the top 150 in nine-cat.
changed: Castle’s role remains the same due to his athleti- cism and defensive ability. With the Spurs using the draft and free agency to primarily address their frontcourt, playing time won’t be an issue for Castle as long as he’s healthy.
outlook: While the Spurs are likely to free up additional minutes for Dylan Harper in his second NBA season, that is unlikely to come at Castle’s expense. He’s good enough defensively to play major minutes, but fantasy managers will want to see Castle take better care of the basketball. Using a fifth- or sixth-round pick to select him won’t be a reach, as the athletic guard still has not reached his full potential.

recap: The second overall pick in the 2025 draft, Harper missed ten games in November after suffering a strained left calf. While his role remained the same upon returning to action, it took Harper some time to hit his stride. After the All-Star break, he averaged 13.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.3 three-pointers per game, coming off the bench in 21 of 25 appearances. Harper’s productivity increased in the postseason, and his fearless nature helped the Spurs reach the NBA Finals. There was some frustration with his role, but Harper never let that affect his play.
changed: Nothing has changed regarding the Spurs’ pe- rimeter rotation, as De’Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle remain. Unless the Spurs decide to move Devin Vassell or Julian Champagnie to the bench, Harper is likely to come off the bench again in 2026-27.
outlook: Coming off the bench had a major impact on Harper’s fantasy value, as he hovered around the top 200 in eight- and nine-cat formats as a rookie. While the expectation is that he’ll be better and pick up additional minutes, Harper’s fantasy ceiling is limited when used as the sixth man. Using a pick just inside the top 100 on Harper may be a bit of a reach, but he has the skill set to make good on those expectations.

recap: In two-plus seasons with the Timberwolves, Alexander-Walk- er emerged as one of the top reserves in the NBA. However, when Minne- sota couldn’t give him the contract he earned, the guard signed with the Hawks as a free agent. While Alexander-Walker began last season as a reserve, it didn’t take long for Hawks head coach Quin Snyder to make him a starter, and that change happened before Trae Young went down with a knee injury. NAW remained a starter for the rest of the season, earning Most Improved Player honors and being close to a top 25 player in fantasy basketball.
changed: Regarding Alexander-Walker’s role, nothing has changed. He should start in the backcourt alongside CJ McCollum and Dyson Daniels as the Hawks look to build on their 46-win 2025-26 season. However, the Hawks added another defensive menace in Luguentz Dort, which could give Alexander-Walker a slight boost in the defensive cate- gories, and lottery pick Kingston Flemings could be the long-term answer at point guard.
outlook: How sustainable was Alexander-Walker’s first season in At- lanta? That’s the question fantasy managers will have to ask themselves when considering whether to select him in drafts. The role makes it real- istic to expect middle-round value, with a shot at cracking the top 50 if everything breaks in NAW’s favor. Anthony Edwards Photo by Scott Wachter-Imagn Images

recap: For the fourth time in five NBA seasons, Suggs failed to reach 60 games, appearing in 57. While his scoring average decreased by just over two points per game in comparison to 2024-25, the 6-foot-5 guard re- corded career-high averages in assists and steals. Due to those improve- ments, with Suggs averaging 2.5 steals+blocks per game, he was close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats. The good news for fantasy managers was that most of his availability issues occurred early in the season, with Suggs missing just five games between February 1 and the end of the regular season.
changed: For the first time in his NBA career, Suggs will be playing for someone other than Jamahl Mosley. With the Magic once again failing to get out of the first round, Mosley was fired, with former Spurs assistant Sean Sweeney taking over.
outlook: Most of the Magic rotation from a season ago is unchanged; the front office is betting on internal improvements. Given how well the Spurs guards played last season, there will be hope that Sweeney’s ar- rival will bode well for Suggs and the other Magic guards. Even with his shooting issues, Suggs’ productivity isn’t a major fantasy concern; avail- ability is. That knocks him down most draft boards, meaning he’s likely to be available in the 85-100 range in standard leagues. As long as he isn’t the primary point guard on a fantasy roster, Suggs will be worth the risk at that point.

recap: After rupturing his Achilles tendon during Milwaukee’s first- round series against the Pacers in the 2025 playoffs, Lillard was waived by the Bucks as the franchise looked to revamp its roster. That opened the door for a return to Portland, even though he could not play. Lillard spent the entirety of the 2025-26 season rehabbing from his injury and will be good to go when the 2026-27 season begins.
changed: With Lillard sidelined, the Trail Blazers reached the postseason for the first time in five years, losing to the Spurs in the first round. While guards Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson are back from that team, Portland also acquired Ja Morant from the Grizzlies, creating a crowded point guard rotation.
outlook: At his best, Lillard has shown in the past an ability to provide elite fantasy value. However, the return from an Achilles injury and Port- land’s many point guards won’t do him any favors. In addition to Morant, Holiday, and Henderson, one also has to consider how well Deni Avdija performed in a playmaking role last season. And there’s the matter of Portland having a new head coach, with Micah Nori taking over for Tiago Splitter. Given the circumstances, selecting Lillard in the sixth or seventh round of a standard league draft would be fair.

recap: Coming off the most productive season of his NBA career at the time, Powell was traded by the Clippers to the Heat last summer. It was a contract year for the veteran guard, and the Clippers were unlikely to give him the payday he sought. After missing out on the All-Star Game in 2024-25, Powell earned the midseason honor for the first time in 2025-26. Unfortunately, injuries limited him to 58 games, and he missed 13 after the break as the Heat finished tenth in the East and missed the postseason. Powell offered top 75 fantasy value, but the availability issues meant that fantasy managers were unable to reap the rewards consistently during the playoff weeks.
changed: Powell did not get his major payday in Miami, as the Heat focused on acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo from the Bucks. He agreed to a two-year deal worth just over $44 million with the Bulls, including a player option for 2027-28.
outlook: Powell will figure prominently in the Bulls’ rotation, which bodes well for his fantasy value. However, he’s appeared in 60 games or fewer in four of the last five seasons. Fantasy managers will need to factor that in when evaluating Powell in drafts. The circumstances make him an intriguing option within the first 75 picks, but it would be wise to wait a bit longer before selecting the veteran in drafts. And younger players like lottery pick Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis will be a higher priority in Chicago than Powell, especially if the Bulls get off to a slow start.

recap: With Jayson Tatum continuing his recovery from a ruptured Achilles tendon and Kristaps Porziņǵis, Jrue Holiday and Al Horford no longer in the picture, Pritchard began the season as a starter. In 48 starts, he averaged 16.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 0.8 steals and 2.5 three-pointers per game. However, after returning to the bench in early February, Pritchard offered a little more as a scorer, averaging 17.0 points and 2.9 three-pointers in his final 31 regular-season games. In nine-cat formats, Pritchard’s production aligned with his preseason ADP (72).
changed: The big change in Boston was the Celtics’ decision to trade Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia in a package that sent Paul George and future draft compensation to Beantown. Tatum being fully healthy and being able to focus on his craft is another change that impacts Pritchard.
outlook: Whether he starts or comes off the bench, Pritchard has reached a point where he can be relied on to offer consistent fantasy val- ue. However, his ADP should not change much, if at all, when compared to where it was last fall. Pritchard will play plenty, but the fantasy ceiling is limited with Tatum, George and Derrick White all due to have the ball in their hands plenty.

recap: VanVleet entered what essentially amounted to a contract year, with his 2026-27 salary being a player option. Unfortunately, the vet- eran point guard never saw the court, as a torn ACL suffered just before training camp ended his season before it even began. While the Rockets left the door open for a return at some point during the 2025-26 campaign, it never happened.
changed: VanVleet, who is back to full strength, picked up his player option worth $25 million this summer. He’ll be an unrestricted free agent in 2027.
outlook: Even with the low field-goal percentage, with VanVleet shoot- ing just 40.1 percent for his career, he can offer excellent fantasy value. Having the opportunity to play off a scorer of the caliber of Kevin Durant should get him cleaner looks, especially from beyond the arc. Expecting VanVleet to offer a top 50 season in 2026-27 may be a bit much, but fantasy managers should not sleep on him. The injury is likely to push him down draft boards, opening the door for VanVleet to be one of the most valuable picks outside the top 100.

recap: Limited to 36 games as a rookie, Mitchell once again had to deal with injuries. An abdominal strain in late January sidelined the guard for 20 games, and he didn’t return until March 9. Mitchell, who finished fifth in Sixth Man of the Year voting, experienced increases in all of his averages and was close to a top 100 player in category leagues. However, the time missed is why he was available in nearly 80 percent of Yahoo! leagues.
changed: Oklahoma City felt the need to avoid the second apron, so some of the players Mitchell competed with for rotation minutes are no longer in the picture. Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins are now in Atlanta, while Isaiah Joe was traded to the Pistons.
outlook: Mitchell’s fantasy outlook in 2026-27 depends on two factors: whether he starts and his health. He made 16 starts last season while Cason Wallace made 58, and that may be a clue into head coach Mark Daigneault’s thinking as he looks to account for Dort’s departure. How- ever, whether he starts or comes off the bench, a healthy Mitchell will have the opportunities needed to offer increased fantasy value. Fantasy managers won’t have to reach for him within the first 100 picks in most drafts, but Mitchell will be worth a look just past that point.

recap: While the offensive output did not improve much, Wallace fur- ther cemented himself as one of the top perimeter defenders in the NBA. Earning second-team All-Defense honors, the 6-foot-3 guard averaged a career-best 1.9 steals per game. Add in the offensive production, and Wal- lace was close to a top 100 player in category leagues. And with some of the moves Oklahoma City made this offseason, his fantasy ceiling will be higher going into 2026-27.
changed: While Wallace remains in Oklahoma City, a few of the players he competed with for rotation minutes do not. Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins were traded to Atlanta in separate deals, while Isaiah Joe was moved to Detroit. Those transactions should free up more minutes for Wallace, who will be extension-eligible until a few days before opening night.
outlook: Whether or not Wallace and the Thunder agree to an exten- sion before the season begins should not be of concern to fantasy manag- ers. If something does happen, his future will be secure, while the lack of a new deal could serve as motivation. Dort’s exit opens a spot in the starting lineup, with either Wallace or Ajay Mitchell being the likely replacement. If it’s Wallace, playing off of stars Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Wil- liams more would open up additional catch-and-shoot opportunities, po- tentially increasing his three-point production. Starting would increase Wallace’s chances of offering top 100 value, but he should be selected outside of that threshold in drafts.

recap: Signed by the Grizzlies to a three-year deal worth nearly $28 million, Jerome appeared headed for a prominent role within the team’s rotation. However, a high-grade calf strain suffered during the preseason delayed his debut until January 31. Jerome would appear in just 15 games before being ruled out for the rest of the season in late March. While valu- able when available, Jerome didn’t play enough to consistently help fan- tasy managers.
changed: Jerome being healthy is one significant change for the Grizzlies’ point guard. The other was Memphis moving on from Ja Morant, which likely puts the keys to the offense in Jerome’s hands.
outlook: While he did finish last season with career-best averages in points, rebounds, assists and three-pointers, that doesn’t mean much when you only play 15 games. Jerome has been healthy this summer, which, along with Morant’s exit, has pushed him up draft boards. The cir- cumstances make him worthy of being selected within the first 100 picks in standard league drafts, but the approach does come with some risk, as Jerome has hit 70 games once in his NBA career. As long as he isn’t their team’s first point guard option, managers who select Jerome should be fine.

recap: McCollum began last season in Washington, playing for a franchise that was clearly prioritizing its draft lottery odds. His average of nearly 20 points per game between December 1 and January 6 fac- tored into the Wizards going 8-9 over a 17-game stretch, and that’s when the plug was pulled. McCollum was sent to Atlanta as part of a deal that sent Trae Young to the nation’s capital, getting the veteran guard onto a team with playoff ambitions. While McCollum began his time in Atlanta as a reserve, he moved into the starting lineup for good after the All-Star break. The Hawks went 20-5 after the break, with McCollum averaging 18.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.4 three-pointers per game during this stretch.
changed: McCollum, whose play helped the Hawks hand the eventual champion Knicks two of their three postseason defeats, agreed to a one-year deal worth $21 million to remain in Atlanta. His role should remain the same, with the veteran guard starting alongside Nickeil Alex- ander-Walker.
outlook: While his fantasy ceiling may not be what it was during his days in Portland, McCollum is capable of providing consistent value. How- ever, using a top 100 pick on him would be unnecessary, whether it’s in a category league or points league. McCollum should be available outside of that threshold, making him a solid value pick in the latter rounds of standard league drafts.

recap: One of the most highly regarded freshmen in college basket- ball, Peterson averaged 20.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.4 steals and 2.6 three-pointers per game in his lone season at Kansas. However, avail- ability concerns lingered, with mysterious maladies limiting him to 24 of the Jayhawks’ 35 games. There was some concern that this would impact Peterson’s standing on draft boards, but that would not be the case.
changed: Peterson was selected by the Jazz with the second overall pick in the 2025 draft.
outlook: Peterson considers point guard to be his long-term position in the NBA, but Keyonte George is coming off the most productive season of his career and may hold onto that role for years to come in Utah. Can they play alongside each other? That will likely need to be the case if Pe- terson expects to play starters’ minutes as a rookie. And that would likely require the Jazz to either move Ace Bailey out of the starting lineup or start Jaren Jackson Jr. at center, with the latter being more effective as a power forward. Playing time should not be an issue for Peterson, but his fantasy ceiling as a rookie may be limited compared to some of the other rookies entering the league. Tyrese Maxey Photo by Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images

recap: Podziemski was the lone Warrior to play in all 82 games, and one of two (Gary Payton II) to appear in at least 70 games last season. Mak- ing 43 starts, he posted career-best averages in points and three-pointers while matching his previous high in assists and steals. From March 1 on- ward, Podziemski averaged 18.1 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.5 three-pointers per game while shooting 47.5 percent from the field and 83.8 percent from the foul line. Even with a healthy Stephen Curry, the Warriors are likely to need similar production from Podziemski if they’re to reach the postseason after failing to do so last season.
changed: Podziemski’s situation is unchanged, as he will once again figure prominently in the Warriors’ rotation. However, with Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody still recovering from serious knee injuries, Podziemski should have even more leeway within Steve Kerr’s system.
outlook: With Butler and Moody highly unlikely to be available to begin the season, Podziemski should open the season as a starter. If so, that opens the door for him to provide greater value than some ex- pect, possibly creeping into the top 100. However, when drafting, fantasy managers have to consider what may happen over the entire season, not just the start. With that being the case, Podziemski is someone who should be targeted just outside the first 100 picks, regardless of league format.

recap: The 11th overall pick in the 2025 draft, Coward was a full go despite his final college season being limited to three games due to a torn labrum. While he wouldn’t move into the starting lineup until mid-Novem- ber, the 6-foot-5 guard averaged nearly 14 points per game in his first 34 appearances. A right knee injury would sideline Coward for seven games in February, and he appeared in just 12 games after the All-Star break. The good news is that Coward was fully available in Summer League, playing in both events the Grizzlies participated in.
changed: This summer marked the end of an era in Mem- phis, as the Grizzlies moved on from Ja Morant and Santi Aldama. Coward stepped up as a leader over the summer, and he’ll be expected to fill that role next season as part of a rotation that will include lottery pick Cameron Boozer.
outlook: Coward did not hit his ADP (102) as a rookie, but he did of- fer late-round value in standard leagues when available. Given the roster changes, fantasy managers will expect more from him going into his sec- ond season. However, opposing teams will pay more attention to Coward, which could make for some challenging moments early on. While not a lock to be a top 100 pick in drafts, fantasy managers should not let Coward fall too far past that threshold.

recap: After appearing in all 82 regular-season games each of his final two seasons in Houston, Green’s first run in Phoenix was limited due to injuries. He initially suffered a strained hamstring during training camp and aggravated it just before the start of the regular season. After missing eight games, Green made his Suns debut on November 6, going off for 30 points in a win over the Clippers. Unfortunately, he would aggravate the hamstring injury two nights later, missing more than two months of ac- tion. The good news is that Green only missed two games after the All-Star break, the final two of the regular seasons, but the hamstring issues did serious damage to his fantasy value.
changed: Some of the pieces around Green have changed. The Suns acquired Miles Bridges from the Hornets in a deal that sent re- serves Grayson Allen and Royce O’Neale to Charlotte, and they signed pe- rimeter marksman Luke Kennard in free agency.
outlook: When healthy, Green can be a solid fantasy asset in points leagues, while the category league value is limited due to lackluster pro- duction outside of points and three-pointers. Devin Booker is clearly the top offensive option, while Bridges’ addition means there’s another scorer to be accounted for. And Dillon Brooks, whose offensive role expanded last season due to Green’s absences, can’t be overlooked, either. The hope for fantasy managers will be that Green rebounds with a top 100 season, but he can’t be selected that early in drafts. It would be best to target him just outside of that threshold.

recap: After playing inconsistent minutes as a rookie, Sheppard took on a more prominent role last season due largely to Fred VanVleet going down with a torn ACL. Appearing in all 82 games, the 6-foot-2 guard start- ed 21 and finished sixth in Sixth Man of the Year voting. Sheppard finished having improved his averages across the board, including 1.5 steals and 2.8 three-pointers per game. As a result, he provided top 100 value in cat- egory leagues while ranking outside of that threshold in points leagues.
changed: The most significant change for Sheppard is that VanVleet will be back on the court, likely pushing him to the bench.
outlook: VanVleet’s return lowers Sheppard’s fantasy ceiling, but he remains a key player for the Rockets, especially in the future. FVV will be an unrestricted free agent next summer, and the play of both players will affect the thinking of the Rockets’ front office. As evidenced by his produc- tion last season, Sheppard is more than capable of returning top 100 fanta- sy value, if not top 75. However, VanVleet’s presence makes it challenging to commit a top 100 pick to Sheppard in redraft leagues.

recap: Dosunmu began his fifth NBA season with the Bulls, appear- ing in 45 games before being traded to the Timberwolves at the February deadline. In 24 regular-season appearances for Minnesota, he averaged 14.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.5 three-pointers per game. And with the team hit hard by injuries, Dosunmu answered the call during the postseason, totaling 68 points in Games 3 and 4 of Minnesota’s first-round series with Denver. Dosunmu himself was in- jured during Game 5, missing the series clincher and the first game of the Timberwolves’ second-round series against the Spurs, which San Antonio won in five games.
changed: Dosunmu appeared poised to be a starter to begin next season following Donte DiVincenzo’s Achilles tendon rup- ture, especially after agreeing to a five-year, $112 million deal to remain in Minnesota. However, two other Timberwolves transactions changed that. In addition to acquiring LaMelo Ball from the Hornets, the Tim- berwolves signed forward Jonathan Kuminga to a two-year deal. While those moves may consign Dosunmu to the bench, he should still play plenty.
outlook: During his time in Chicago, Dosunmu was usually a player who fantasy managers would take a late-round flier on in drafts. He should go a little earlier than that in drafts this fall, but the arrivals of Ball and Kuminga aren’t great news for those hoping that Dosunmu’s value would take a significant jump. Ayo is a player who fantasy managers should con- sider just outside the first 100 picks in standard league drafts, hoping that his value will exceed the ADP.

recap: When available, Porter proved to be surprisingly valuable to fantasy managers. His per-game averages made him a second-round player in category leagues. However, Porter played just 38 games, limit- ing the return fantasy managers got from rostering him. A serious ankle sprain suffered during the Bucks’ season-opener sidelined KPJ for just over a month, and he missed six games in late January with a strained oblique. Porter appeared in just four games after March 1, seeing his last game action on March 17 before a knee injury ended his season.
changed: There were multiple changes, starting with Por- ter’s decision to pick up his player option worth nearly $5.4 million. The Bucks also traded Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Heat, with the return including guards Tyler Herro and Kasparas Jakučionis. Gary Trent Jr. was re-signed, and Milwaukee used one of its two lottery picks on Arizona guard Brayden Burries. Lastly, Taylor Jenkins was hired as the new head coach, replacing Doc Rivers.
outlook: While Porter being healthy is good news, his fantasy ceiling is limited due to the logjam in the Bucks’ perimeter rotation. Who the team prioritizes remains to be seen, but younger players like Burries and Ryan Rollins may be the focus as the franchise embarks on a new era. And this doesn’t take into consideration the fact that Herro, like Porter, is in a contract year. As shown last season when he was available, Porter can provide excellent fantasy value, but his role may not align with the one he enjoyed in 2025-26.

recap: Most of Tatum’s 2025-26 campaign was spent rehabbing an Achilles tear. His eventual return to the floor came after the All-Star Break, where he logged 16 regular-season games. Understandably, there was a vast amount of rust, and although we saw glimpses of the pre-in- jury version of Tatum, he finished the season averaging 21.8 points on 41.1/32.9/82.3 shooting splits. He made up for his shooting inconsistencies by remaining a strong facilitator (5.3 assists per game) and logging a ca- reer-best 10.0 boards per game.
changed: The Celtics shook up their roster by trading away 2024 Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for veteran forward Paul George. George and Tatum have fairly similar builds and offer similar playing styles. Theoretically, another season removed from the Achilles tear and now without Brown, Tatum’s usage should creep up a notch as more will be on his plate. The only question now is: can he return to form and deliver another top 10 or top 20 finish in 9-cat leagues?
outlook: Even if Tatum doesn’t quite reach the same level that he did in either the 2022-23 or 2023-24 seasons, it’s hard to imagine him not improving on his 2025-26 performance. Again, Brown’s departure should result in an uptick in usage for Tatum, and a bump in minutes should also be in store as he moves farther away from the Achilles tear. He should be in for a bounceback season so long as injuries are a non-concern.

recap: The 2021 first-round pick turned out his best season as a pro- fessional and was rewarded with a spot in the 2026 NBA All-Star Game. Johnson, as he has consistently, improved as a scorer, rebounder, and facilitator, topping 20 points per game for the first time while tallying 10.3 rebounds and 7.9 assists per game. He experienced growing pains in Atlanta’s first-round exit to the eventual champion New York Knicks but given his year-by-year strides over the regular season, should be in a tre- mendous spot to make another leap in Year 6.
changed: On the surface, not much. The Hawks retained vet- eran guard CJ McCollum and will likely trot out the same starting lineup on opening night that they ended the postseason with. Their wing depth expanded with the offseason additions of Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Kingston Flemmings, but neither of those guys should eat into the minutes or usage that Johnson figures to have for the 2026-27 season.
outlook: Johnson could realistically finish as a top 10 player in 9-cat leagues, with potential to creep into the top 5, so long as injuries aren’t an issue. Even with how productive he’s been, there are clear areas for improvement that could boost his rankings this upcoming season — con- tinued and increased three-point production, and a return to form as a disruptive defender who routinely collects stocks. Expectations are de- servedly high for the former Duke Blue Devil in both the fantasy basketball world and non-fantasy reality.

recap: The expectations were high for the 2025 No. 1 overall pick, and while it took him a little time to figure things out, Flagg proved to be a star before his first season concluded. He ended up winning Rookie of the Year and had some monster performances throughout the season. Flagg exceeded sky-high expectations, and he is still only 19 years old, making him younger than nine lottery picks from this past draft.
changed: After missing all of last season, Kyrie Irving will be back and ready to assist Flagg as a ball handler and scorer. Dallas also has a new head coach, with Dusty May taking over a few days before the draft after winning a national championship at Michigan last year. The Mavs have more depth in the frontcourt, with Morez Johnson Jr., Santi Aldama and Zaccharie Risacher all joining the team this summer. However, this team is built around Flagg. He’ll remain the focal point, with everyone else there to support him.
outlook: Once again, the expectations for Flagg are incredibly high. Just like they were ahead of last season, and just like they were ahead of his lone season at Duke. He has already shown he can provide value in every category, and he did it while shooting a low percentage from the floor, especially down the stretch when his usage rate was off the charts. The influx of talent should open things up for Flagg, who should show the growth that is generally seen from players as they enter their second season in the league. Don’t be surprised if Flagg exceeds expectations once again.

recap: Barnes had a fairly similar 2025-26 season to his prior two campaigns. Notably, he was on the floor for more than 65 games for the first time since his second season as a professional and shot 50 per- cent from the field for the first time in his career. Three-point shooting remained a struggle and there wasn’t much statistical progression across the stat sheet. Overall, Barnes turned in a familiar fantasy season, but per- haps his performance in the most recent postseason could carry into the upcoming season.
changed: Now that the NBA’s investigation into Kawhi Leon- ard and the LA Clippers has concluded, the next step is for the Clippers and Raptors to complete their agreed-upon trade for the two-time Finals MVP. Assuming that happens, Barnes will share the floor with another of- fensive engine who’s coming off arguably his best regular season since his 2018-19 season in Toronto. Leonard’s gravity and offensive skillset should open up the game for Barnes to grow but also allow him to con- tinue to soak up usage. Perhaps some of the defensive responsibility that Leonard assumes will also save some legs and energy for Barnes on the offensive end.
outlook: The superstar trajectory has potentially passed Barnes by, even being just 25 years of age. That said, he’s very clearly an All-Star who can have superstar moments, as shown in last season’s playoff series against the Cleveland Cavaliers. Expect more of the same from Barnes this upcoming season that he’s consistently shown over the past three campaigns — hovering somewhere in the range of 20 points, sev- en rebounds, and six assists per game, with his usual production on the defensive end.

recap: From the outside looking in, there seemed to be a lot going on in Houston that ultimately led to a relatively disappointing season for the Rockets. Yet, like clockwork, the two-time Finals MVP turned in another superb individual season. He efficiently shot his way into 26 points per game while remaining a solid contributor as a passer and rebounder. Most importantly, Durant logged 78 regular-season games — the most he’s finished a regular season with since his final year with the Golden State Warriors. His good injury luck unfortunately expired at the end of the regular season, as an ankle injury kept him from participating in the postseason.
changed: The Rockets should have more backcourt help this year — Fred VanVleet will likely be recovered from an ACL tear and be healthy enough to be in the opening-night lineup, and the offseason addition of Marcus Smart could take some of the load off Durant on both ends of the floor. In theory, these additions should let Durant expend a bit less energy and take on fewer playmaking responsibilities, potentially lowering his turnover output and freeing him up to score more.
outlook: As mentioned above, Durant was the healthiest last season that he’s been in years. If the veteran can manage his body well enough to make it through the fantasy basketball season, there’s no reason to expect a drop-off in production. His game has aged beautifully, and Father Time hasn’t quite caught up to him yet.

recap: Quietly, Leonard logged his best statistical season in 2025-26 since his lone campaign in Toronto. He’ll head back to Canada having av- eraged 27.9 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.9 steals, and 2.6 three-point- ers per game on 50.5/38.7/89.2 shooting splits. The scoring and three- point production marked new career highs, which is impressive for a player who’s dealt with as many injuries as Leonard has throughout his career.
changed: The two-time Finals MVP returns to where he earned arguably his career-defining achievement. He’ll join another in- his-prime superstar for the first time in several years, which could offer a range of outcomes with regard to his production and style of play.
outlook: There weren’t many players last season who were as good as Leonard at putting the ball in the basket. Given what we know about his injury history, is it realistic to expect both his level of play and the number of games he plays in his return season to Toronto? He actually finds himself in a great position, with several pieces around him that fit well enough to make his production sustainable. We’ll see how the cookie crumbles.

recap: With all the rumors surrounding a potential trade for Gi- annis, this ended up being one of his least productive seasons in a long time. To be clear, that wasn’t because his play dropped off. Per posses- sion, it was actually one of the best seasons of his career, specifically as a scorer. Unfortunately, he played fewer than 60 games for the first time in his career, and his minutes were the lowest they’ve been since his rookie year.
changed: Well, after years of rumors, the Giannis trade final- ly came to fruition, with Miami winning the sweepstakes. With the Heat, Antetokounmpo should return to his typical minutes allocation and con- tinue to be the focal point on offense. That should help his production in the box score across the board after a disappointing season.
outlook: For the past decade, Giannis has been one of the best play- ers in fantasy basketball, assuming you can deal with the poor free throw shooting and lack of three-pointers. With his new team, there’s no rea- son to think that won’t continue. He should be one of the first few picks in points leagues, and he should still go in the middle of the first round in category formats. Coming off a forgettable season, expect Giannis to return to form with a chip on his shoulder while playing outside of Mil- waukee for the first time in his career. There are plenty of talented players around him, but this Heat team currently lacks depth, meaning they’ll lean on Antetokounmpo a ton.

recap: The lasting taste of a four-point Game 7 performance in Okla- homa City’s Western Conference Finals loss to the San Antonio Spurs is likely what jumps to the front of mind for many when Holmgren’s name surfaces. Instead, what should be highlighted is the strong campaign that the 7-footer out of Gonzaga put together. Holmgren proved he could stay healthy, playing 69 regular-season games, and still set career highs in points and rebounds per game while maintaining production as a shot blocker.
changed: Short answer: not a lot. The Thunder re-upped with starting center Isaiah Hartenstein to pair alongside Holmgren in the frontcourt and added more size off the bench when drafting Aday Mara out of Michigan. Some roster tweaks in the backcourt may change a bit of OKC’s process, but nothing that should impact Holmgren’s role or produc- tion on a nightly basis.
outlook: There’s still room for statistical progression. After proving good health a season ago, Holmgren could average more than 30 minutes per game for the first time as a pro, allowing him to capitalize on his effi- cient shooting and well-documented two-way ability. He may also have a chip on his shoulder based on how his 2025-26 campaign ended.

recap: Needless to say, it was a year to forget for Williams. Offseason wrist surgery delayed his start to the season by a month, and a right ham- string injury forced him to miss nearly two months of games from January to March. He returned before the start of the playoffs, and they managed his minutes leading up to the postseason, but a left hamstring injury in the first round resulted in him only playing in five playoff games. His produc- tion took a big hit because he was never fully healthy.
changed: After an injury-riddled season, Williams should be healthy to start this upcoming season, which is important. He won’t need a ramp-up period to be ready to play; Williams should be ready to roll on opening night. OKC didn’t make any big swings this offseason, which means Williams should be closer to the role he played two years ago, when he played 32.4 minutes per game.
outlook: Expect a bounce-back season from Williams. He’s been a well-rounded fantasy stud whenever he’s been healthy throughout his ca- reer. The Thunder have plenty of depth, but Williams is the second option on this team. Injuries prevented him from getting in a rhythm last season, but being healthy from day one, and during training camp, should make a big difference for him. Williams was a top 25 player in fantasy basketball two seasons ago and should get back to that level of production.

recap: There’s not much to gather from Davis’ 2025-26 season other than the fact that he missed most of it due to injury. He played 20 games with the Dallas Mavericks before being shipped to the Nation’s Capital, where he never set foot on the court for the Washington Wizards. The for- mer first-overall pick of the 2013 NBA Draft has totaled only 71 games over the past two seasons, 29 since being dealt to the Mavericks in a block- buster trade that sent Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers. Injuries aside, Davis’ scoring production has fallen off when he’s been able to suit up and log minutes. He averaged 20.4 points over his 20 games in Dallas last season despite shooting 50.6 percent from the field. He remains a double-double threat with defensive upside in fantasy leagues, despite no longer being as dominant on that end of the floor.
