changed: Realistically, a lot has changed for Davis, as he has yet to play a game for the Wizards despite having been traded there in the middle of last season. He’ll function as a pick-and-roll partner with Trae Young and will play alongside another No. 1-overall pick, AJ Dybantsa, for an organization in the middle of a retooling. There are a lot of unknowns ahead of the start of training camp.
outlook: Assuming good health, Davis is likely to soak up his usual share of minutes in the starting frontcourt, which should lead to consis- tent 20-10 double-doubles with a few stocks for good measure. But you simply can’t assume good health at this point in his career. He’s a high-up- side player with obvious availability issues that could come back to bite fantasy managers if his body can’t maintain.

recap: Murphy peaked at the start of the calendar year when he averaged 24.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.1 assists, and 3.6 three-pointers in 14 January games, only to follow it with 27.4 points and 5.6 triples per game in February. The surrounding months were relatively mediocre, but his mid-season dominance ultimately helped him set new career-high averages for a single season in points, rebounds, assists, steals, and three-pointers — he accomplished this in 66 regular-season games, also a new career high.
changed: Despite being a popular name in the offseason trade rumors, Murphy is staying put in New Orleans for the time being. His surrounding cast could look fairly similar, with Zion Williamson, Her- bert Jones, Jeremiah Fears, and others back for another season, with Ben- nedict Mathurin being the key offseason addition. Perhaps the biggest change came on the sideline, as New Orleans hired Jamahl Mosley to be their head coach. Mosley’s schemes and ideas could bring change, but without much significant roster turnover, Murphy is set to play another significant role on both ends of the floor for the Pelicans.
outlook: Murphy has seen his production increase each year since being drafted in 2021. Now entering Year 6, and potentially the start of his prime, there’s no reason to doubt more progression is on the way. Even if the uptick in production is incremental once again, he should be New Or- leans’ most productive player from a fantasy standpoint, and a borderline top 10 player at his position.

recap: Mobley’s 2025-26 campaign wasn’t all that different from his 2024-24 season. His counting stats were nearly identical over both regular seasons, but the efficiency took a notable dip. The former No. 3-overall pick saw his three-point field-goal percentage sink under 30.0 percent for the first time since his second NBA season, which was quite different from the 37 percent he logged in each of the two prior seasons. He’s also got to the charity stripe more times on average than he had ever before, but a career-worst 60.6 percent left him unable to fully capitalize.
changed: For the most part, Cleveland’s core will remain intact. Max Strus’ departure to Los Angeles, coinciding with Peyton Wat- son’s arrival, shouldn’t have much of an impact on Mobley’s fantasy value. However, James Harden will get a full offseason and training camp to build on his connection with the Cavaliers scorers, which should benefit Mobley as the season progresses.
outlook: The former Defensive Player of the Year should, again, be a force on that end of the floor, and if he can bounce back from a scoring ef- ficiency standpoint, there’s a real chance that he concludes as one of the top handful of power forwards. He’ll be one of several Cavaliers starters with potential to make a sizeable fantasy basketball impact.

recap: Avdija followed up on a strong finish to the 2024-25 season with his best season as a pro last year. He posted career highs in points, assists and three-pointers per game, which led to his first All-Star appear- ance and had him finish in the top three for the Most Improved Player award. Avdija’s leap also helped Portland return to the playoffs for the first time since the 2020-2021 season.
changed: Although Avdija will still be made a priority on this team, Damian Lillard will be healthy after missing all of last season with a torn Achilles. The Blazers also made a trade for Ja Morant, and they still re- tained Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, giving them plenty of ball-han- dling and playmaking options. However, they’re thin at the forward spots outside of Avdija and Toumani Camara.
outlook: The inflated assist numbers that Avdija posted last season will likely take a hit with all the talented point guards that will be joining the rotation. A usage drop will likely reduce Avdija’s fantasy impact, but the added help should allow him to be more effective in other categories. Only Luka Doncic averaged more turnovers per game than Avdija last sea- son, which should be cleaned up with the ball in his hands less. Plus, other playmakers should give Avdija some easier shots, which will help his field goal percentage. While his value shouldn’t be totally decimated, it’s diffi- cult to project a scenario where he is as impactful as he was last season.

recap: A couple days before last season’s trade deadline, Jackson was dealt to Utah after spending the first 7.5 seasons of his career in Mem- phis. He only played in three games for Utah before being shut down due to a left knee injury. Prior to the deal, he wasn’t having a great season for the Grizzlies, with his scoring taking a hit from the two prior seasons. It was a season to forget for managers that drafted him.
changed: Though he has already suited up for the Jazz a few times, this will basically be a fresh start for Jackson. He’ll likely be starting next to Lauri Markkanen and Jusuf Nurkic in the frontcourt on a team that was second in the NBA in pace last season. What was arguably Jackson’s best offensive season came during the 2024-25 season, when the Grizzlies led the league in pace. This is an offense that is set up for him to have success, and he has a big man next to him that will allow him to focus on being a versatile defender.
outlook: There was a time when Jackson was heralded as one of the most valuable pieces in dynasty leagues. However, a drop in block production, combined with inconsistent scoring and poor rebounding has desecrated his image in fantasy hoops. What Utah has been cook- ing up over the last few years might be just what Jackson needs to get back to fantasy star status. This is arguably the most talented offensive team he’s been on, even if most of that talent is pretty young. Jackson shouldn’t have to force the issue on offense, which may help his effi- ciency, but his defense will be vital to this team’s success. As long as he can safely stay out of foul trouble, Jackson could have one of the best seasons of his career.

recap: After a down year during the 2024-25 season, Markkanen bounced back in a big way last season, which included him setting a new career high for points per game. Unfortunately, injuries to his right hip and right ankle ended his season early. He only played one game after the All- Star break, which was a new career low for him. He was one of the best players in fantasy basketball when he was healthy, but he wasn’t available enough, or at the right times, for it to matter.
changed: Following a few years of tanking, the Jazz seem ready to finally make a push for the postseason. With Utah focused on winning, they should be a bit more willing to let Markkanen play through injuries. Markkanen’s games played have gone down every season he’s been with the Jazz, but that number should go up, which should make Markkanen more valuable in fantasy basketball.
outlook: While there have been red flags when drafting Markkanen ahead of the last few seasons, there shouldn’t be many ahead of this year. However, early ADP data shows that Markkanen is being selected in the fourth round, which is incredible value for a player as talented and pro- ductive as he is. He has finished in the top 20 in 9-cat leagues in three of the last four seasons in terms of per-game value, and he should finally have the availability to match. He could end up as one of the better value picks in the top 50.

recap: It doesn’t get much better than the 2025-26 season for Anunoby. He saw his minutes reduced slightly, but he improved his efficiency from the season prior and enjoyed the second-best fantasy finish of his career. Anunoby was instrumental in the Knicks’ postseason success, averaging 20.1 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.6 triples and 2.6 “stocks” while operating as the second-best player on a championship team. He was the hero of Game 4 of the Finals, as his tip-in shot in the final sec- onds gave New York the lead and sealed a decisive victory in a contest that swung the series.
changed: Not much. The Knicks lost Mitchell Robinson and added Andre Drummond to back up Karl-Anthony Towns at center, but the reigning champs will run it back with essentially the same lineup.
outlook: Anunoby finished as a top 60 fantasy option for the fifth time in the last seven seasons on his way to winning a second NBA title. An efficient shooter and three-and-D specialist, Anunoby has fifth-round up- side once again due to his contributions across multiple categories. He’s elite in steals, but otherwise, he’s a solid contributor who doesn’t hurt you badly anywhere. He’s played at least 67 games in three of his last four seasons, and his multi-cat consistency and reliable availability give him a sturdy floor in fantasy hoops.

recap: An oblique injury derailed Wagner’s 2024-25 season, which could’ve been an All-Star season for him if he was healthy. Last season, it was an ankle injury that ruined his year. Wagner only suited up four times between Sep. 8 and the end of March. That absence prevented him from being at full strength entering the postseason, and then he suffered a calf injury in the first round, which kept him sidelined for Games 5-7, resulting in Orlando blowing a 3-1 lead over Detroit.
changed: The Magic fired Jamahl Mosely this offseason and replaced him with Sean Sweeney, who has been an assistant coach in the NBA for a while, most recently with the Spurs. A change in leadership could be just what the Magic need if he can figure out how to maximize all the talent he has to work with.
outlook: Hopes are high in Orlando, and a lot of that is based on the assumption that Sweeney will be a coaching upgrade. If he can make it work where Wagner, Paolo Banchero and Desmond Bane all thrive, it could be fantasy galore. Wagner’s deep-range shot improved last season after being a struggle during the previous two years. He’s still not an elite marksman, but it gives Sweeney more options to work with. Still, even if Wagner has a healthy season, it’s difficult to imagine him reaching his peak as long as he’s playing alongside Banchero. If Sweeney is able to make that happen, he’ll have a strong case for Coach of the Year.

recap: After only playing 27 games during his sophomore season, Miller was more available during third year in the league, and while they managed his minutes, he was more effective when he was out on the floor. He’s developing into one of the best perimeter shooters in the league, and he gets them up at a high rate. His development, along with other players on the team being healthy and progressing, resulted in Charlotte returning to the postseason for the first time since the 2021-22 season.
changed: The Hornets shipped out LaMelo Ball, and while they got Naz Reid back in the trade, they clearly believe in both Miller and Kon Knueppel taking steps forward. Coby White should slot in as the start- ing point guard, with Dennis Schroder backing him up. Both are effective playmakers, but neither is as talented as LaMelo Ball, which should leave extra usage for Miller.
outlook: It was an interesting move for Charlotte to move away from LaMelo, but they clearly believe in Miller and Knueppel as the future of the franchise. They may still manage Miller’s minutes, but when he’s on the floor, he’ll see plenty of usage. Miller also spent more time on the ball last season than Knueppel and created his own shot at a higher rate, which should translate to success this season with LaMelo now in Minnesota. Miller seems poised for a breakout season, and he should be among the league leaders in three-pointers.

recap: For the first time, LeBron actually took a backseat and de- ferred to other stars on his team in a way that was clear in the box score. Of course, he was still highly effective, but he had the ball in his hands less than he ever has, which led to his lowest usage rate since his rookie sea- son. He still posted well-rounded numbers and was efficient as a scorer, but the lack of volume impacted his fantasy output.
changed: LeBron ended his eight-year tenure with the Lak- ers and decided to move across the country to sign a two-year, $8 million deal with Philadelphia. He’ll still slot in as a starter, but now he’ll have Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown next to him needing shots and touches. Clearly, he signed with a priority to win a championship.
outlook: He’ll turn 42 in December, but LeBron just keeps on ticking. His scoring may take another hit this season with all the other elite scor- ing options next to him, but he’ll still have the ball in his hands when he’s on the floor and be effective with it. There will likely be some growing pains for the 76ers early on as they try to figure out how to get all these stars to play together. However, LeBron has some experience doing that, and his playmaking will be important throughout the season. They’ll cer- tainly utilize him, though they’ll also ensure he’s as fresh as possible for the postseason.

recap: With Jayson Tatum sidelined for most of the season due to a ruptured Achilles, the 2025 Finals MVP showed what he was capable of as the Celtics’ No. 1 option. He enjoyed career highs in points, rebounds and assists while leading the C’s to the No. 2 seed in the East. Brown scored 40+ seven times and tied his career-best in scoring with a 50 burger against the Clippers. He did all of this while playing his most games since 2018-19.
changed: The career Bostonian was dealt to Philadelphia in a surprise trade for Paul George, and Brown will face quite a bit more competition for looks while playing alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and LeBron James.
outlook: Brown finished 29th in 8-cat formats in 2025-26, tied for the best fantasy finish of his career. He’ll be hard pressed to reach the heights he reached in Boston in terms of counting stats, but with so many quality scoring options around him, Brown could see more open looks and im- proved efficiency. An uptick in three-pointers and better FG% could keep Brown in the top 50, but his early ADP is a mid-third-rounder and drafting him there is taking him at his ceiling. There are better values in that range.

recap: Boozer was named AP Player of the Year behind averages of 22.5 points, 10.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 2.0 “stocks” and 1.4 triples as he led Duke to a 35-3 record. His averages were similar in four NCAA tournament games, as the Blue Devils fell to UConn in the Elite 8. After a strong one- and-done season with Duke, Boozer heard his name called third in the NBA Draft.
changed: Boozer had a productive Summer League, averag- ing 18 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.8 “stocks” as the Grizzlies lost a tight contest to the Warriors in the Summer League Final. Can his college and Summer League play translate to success on the NBA court?
outlook: Of all the lottery picks in this year’s draft, Boozer could see the most run for a Grizzlies team in desperate need of frontcourt help. Memphis has struggled to stay healthy at forward and center in recent seasons, and Boozer should see big minutes as a Day 1 starter. Early ADP gives Boozer a seventh-round sticker, and he could be a phenomenal val- ue if he falls outside the top 100.

recap: After winning the Most Improved Player award and leading the league in steals two years ago, Daniels was still productive this past season. His scoring and steals dropped, and his three-point shooting, which was never a strength for him, regressed to a new low for him. How- ever, he made up for it by posting career highs in rebounds and assists, and while he wasn’t the outlier leader in steals per game like he was the year before, he was one steal from matching Cason Wallace for most total steals last season.
changed: The Hawks made some moves to add more depth on the wing, namely adding Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins from the Thunder. That gives Atlanta one of the best perimeter defensive rotations in the league, and while it shouldn’t impact Dyson Daniels’ status as a starter, there is more competition for minutes, which could cut into his playing time slightly.
outlook: Managers should expect more of the same from Daniels this upcoming season. Plenty of steals, a decent amount of boards and dimes, and not many triples. At all. That hurts his value in points leagues, but in the right build in category formats, Daniels can be an incredibly valu- able piece to have. He should once again be among the league leaders in steals, but his continued growth in other areas of his game will allow him to be a more well-rounded producer for fantasy managers.

recap: With Tyrese Haliburton out for the season, Siakam was the focus of Indiana’s offense, and his production was a bit underwhelming. Spicy P had career highs in FGA and 3PA with disappointing efficiency, and he finished the campaign 86th in 8-cat formats, his worst finish since 2017-18. Siakam logged 33.2 minutes per game and made only 62 appear- ances in a season that fantasy managers would surely like to forget.
changed: Haliburton is back, and the Pacers have Ivica Zubac anchoring the frontcourt, but the rest of the roster is virtually un- changed. Siakam will likely see a dip in shots, but his efficiency could improve with Haliburton running the show. The presence of a dedicated big man down low could result in fewer rebounds.
outlook: Siakam’s ADP is just outside the top 40, but the best fantasy finish of his career was 2021-22 when he ended the season 33rd in 8-cat value. That season, Siakam logged a career-best 37.9 minutes and finished with 22.8 points, 8.5 rebounds and 5.3 assists with Toronto. He won’t sniff those numbers in Indy this season and selecting him as an early-to-mid- rounder will lead to disappointment.

recap: For a seventh consecutive season, Ingram averaged at least 20 points on efficient shooting splits. The productive offensive numbers came in a near career-high 77 regular-season games, which was on the heels of an 18-game 2024-25 campaign in which he never touched the floor for the Raptors after having been traded midseason by the Pelicans. A slip in playmaking was the only notable regression for Ingram when compared to recent seasons.
changed: Barring an agreed-upon deal between the Raptors and Clippers falling through, Ingram will return to Los Angeles, where he’ll join a team that’s entering a new chapter. His role shouldn’t change much, however — he’ll likely be the Clippers’ primary scoring option that func- tions as a secondary playmaker within the halfcourt offense. With new teammates and a new coach, schemes could change the specific ways that Ingram is utilized. Nonetheless, there aren’t many on the Clippers’ current roster who are more capable with the ball in their hands.
outlook: For many of the reasons listed above, namely roster con- struction and role, it would be rather surprising if Ingram didn’t eclipse the 20-point mark on a per-game basis by season’s end. Given his respon- sibility, he may also be able to bounce back as a facilitator during the 26-27 season. The bigger question comes down to health. Ingram logged 77 regular-season games last season, but only 18, 64, 45, and 55 in the seasons prior. His availability will be a big part of his fantasy value.

recap: Banchero has been a favorite in points leagues for a while, but his production doesn’t hold up as well in category leagues, even if he made improvements last season. His assists were up from the season be- fore, and he posted career highs in rebounds and free throw percentage. He was better about being a facilitator for the team, which led to fewer shot attempts in points, but he actually started to improve his shot diet. Banchero shot fewer three-pointers and mid-range shots and got to the rim at the highest rate of his career. He also posted his best percentage at the rim. Despite all the improvements, he still takes a lot of mid-range shots, and he isn’t particularly efficient from that range.
changed: The Magic made a head coaching change this off- season, replacing Jamahl Mosley with Sean Sweeney. A fresh voice in the room could be just what Orlando needs to take the next step. Sweeney may be able to optimize Banchero’s talent, which could lead to one of the best fantasy seasons of his career.
outlook: The expectation shouldn’t be that Banchero completely cuts out mid-range shots and shoots over 50 percent from the floor. However, he may continue to take real strides in efficiency while still racking up points, rebounds and assists. He’s still much more valuable in points leagues, but he’s talented enough where a few slight improve- ments could turn him into a stronger option in category leagues. This could certainly be the year where that happens if Sweeney is able to get him to buy in.

recap: For the third straight season, Reid averaged at least 13.5 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.1 triples. His shooting splits over that three-year stretch are an impressive 45/36/73 for a big man, and he offers strong efficiency as a stretch four. Reid’s production as a scorer and three-point specialist helped him finish inside the top 120, but he’ll need to do more across the board to crack the top 100.
changed: Reid was traded to the Hornets as part of the LaMelo Ball deal, and he’ll get a chance to prove himself as a full-time starter in Charlotte after operating as a key reserve for Minnesota over the first seven seasons of his career.
outlook: The 2025 Sixth Man of the Year has excelled off the bench throughout his career, but he’ll step into a starting role with the Hornets, which could lead to a career year. Since 2023, Reid has averaged 17.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2.3 “stocks” and 2.7 triples across 31.4 minutes as a starter. He’ll join a Hornets team that ranks ninth in three- point attempts over the last three seasons and that dealt Miles Bridges to the Suns in the offseason.

recap: While once again playing 82 games, Bridges ended up sac- rificing some usage for the betterment of the team. It worked out well, as he posted his best steal and block numbers since he was in Phoenix, and the Knicks went on to win the NBA Finals. Availability continues to be Bridges’ best ability, but his production did falter down the stretch of the regular season.
changed: New York is mostly running things back with the same squad that just won a championship, with some minor tweaks. Bridges shouldn’t be impacted much by the moves the Knicks made, though his durability will be put to the test now that he is on the wrong side of 30.
outlook: Bridges is one of the safer picks in fantasy basketball. Not because he’s guaranteed to make a huge impact, but because manag- ers know exactly what they’re getting from him. He’s going to contribute decent value across the board and should continue to suit up for every game. He played 4.2 fewer minutes per game last season under head coach Mike Brown, and managers shouldn’t expect to see him get close to the 37.0 minutes per game that he saw under Tom Thibodeau.

recap: George’s 2025-26 season played out similarly to the one prior. A 25-game suspension for violating the NBA’s anti-drug policy was a major factor in the veteran finishing the season with 37 regular-season games to show for — injuries also played a role. There were high highs when George did take the floor, but he ultimately points, rebounds, and assists averages that rivaled a disappointing 2024-25 campaign.
changed: Like so many star players, George was relocated during this offseason, going from Philadelphia to Boston in a blockbuster trade that saw him swap places with former Finals MVP Jaylen Brown. After two relatively disappointing seasons with the Sixers, PG will get a fresh start with the Celtics,
outlook: While clearly not in his prime years ahead of his age 36 sea- son, the nine-time NBA All-Star heads to a Celtics organization where he should be able to thrive in his more reduced role under Head Coach Joe Mazzulla. George is historically one of the NBA’s great three-point shoot- ers, and his increased volume over the years hasn’t impacted his efficien- cy. The three-point shot has accounted for around half of George’s shot diet in recent years, which should remain the case in Boston. At the very least, fantasy managers should be able to count on the veteran for be- yond-the-arc production, with steals and contributions on the glass being bonuses.

recap: MPJ finished just outside the second round in 8-cat fantasy, good for the best finish of his career. In his first season with Brooklyn, Por- ter Jr. posted career highs in points, assists, triples and steals, operating as a focal point for the rebuilding Nets. He appeared in just 52 contests, playing 62 or fewer games for the fifth time in his seven-season career.
changed: Brooklyn acquired Julius Randle in the offseason, adding another high-volume, veteran shooter to the mix, and the Nets drafted Mikel Brown Jr. with the sixth pick in the draft.
outlook: Porter Jr. will have a tough time replicating the numbers he put up a season ago. The arrival of Randle should lead to a dip in points, rebounds and assists, while the addition of lottery pick Mikel Brown Jr. and the ascension of last year’s first-round picks will lead to the same. Porter Jr. should still retain value as a trusted scoring option, but last year’s vol- ume will surely not be there. Durability will once again be a concern given his extensive injury history.

recap: Williamson’s 2025-26 campaign was one of his least statisti- cally productive of his NBA career. He set career-lows in points, rebounds, and field goals per game, while seeing some action off the bench for the first time. He also fell short of the 30-minute-per-game mark for the sec- ond straight season. Still, he shot the ball efficiently, and his downhill style remained effective in earning lots of trips to the charity stripe.
changed: In short — not a lot. The Pels’ rotation shouldn’t look too different from last season. The projected starting unit will include a few of the longer-tenured guys, while the bench makes up younger tal- ent that thrived last year, or new roster additions.
outlook: For all that’s already been said, the good news is that Wil- liamson played in 62 of the Pelicans’ 82 regular-season games last season — the second-most of his career. But as New Orleans continues to retool on the fly and usher in a new crop of talent, there’s a legitimate question of how big the former first-overall pick’s role will be this upcoming season. Health is first and foremost, however. And if fantasy managers can find a way to accept that risk when drafting Williamson, they might be able to get more value out of him than where he’s drafted. Cooper Flagg Photo by Jerome Miron-Imagn Images

recap: Randle’s second season in Minnesota ended up going better than his first. He saw more usage, which led to a jump in points and as- sists without sacrificing efficiency. He got off to a hot start, which led to his first top 100 finish in 9-cat leagues since the 2022-23 season, but his production took a big hit after the All-Star break, leading to him not mak- ing much of an impact during the fantasy playoffs.
changed: In what ended up being a four-team trade, Randle was shipped to Brooklyn this offseason. The trade was expanded to in- clude LaMelo Ball heading to Minnesota, but it was originally a cap-relief deal. Randle goes from a contending team to a lottery team, which may impact his shot diet and usage.
outlook: Brooklyn has an interesting team heading into next season. There are high-volume veterans like Randle and Michael Porter Jr., but there is also a ton of youth on the roster. They’ll be the focus of the orga- nization, but Randle and MPJ should get a ton of shots and usage. Randle has always been a strong source of points, rebounds and assists, but ef- ficiency and a lack of defensive stats have kept him from getting respect in category leagues. However, he should get more than enough touches to provide a ton of value.

recap: For the second time over the last three seasons, LaVine ap- peared in fewer than 40 games. Injuries took a toll on the veteran wing as his scoring average dipped to its lowest mark in eight seasons, and his rebound and assist averages were the lowest of his career. He finished outside the top 100 in per-game fantasy value after finishing inside the top 75 in seven straight seasons.
changed: After finishing with the NBA’s worst record, the Kings selected Darius Acuff with the seventh pick in the NBA Draft. Acuff is viewed as a foundational building block in Sacramento, and his arrival could mean less run for LaVine, if the latter remains on the roster.
outlook: The Kings are reportedly shopping LaVine and Domantas Sabonis as they look to begin a rebuild, and LaVine finds himself in the same situation he was in during the 2024-25 season when the Bulls shipped him to Sac-Town during their rebuild. LaVine has shown top 15 upside, and a fully healthy season could make him a value selection in fantasy drafts if his ADP remains outside the top 100. The team he lands on matters, but even if he stays with the Kings, he’s looking like a prime 2026-27 sleeper candidate.

recap: McDaniels has long been one of the league’s premier defend- ers, but he took an offensive leap this past season. He posted career highs in points, assists, three-point percentage and free-throw percentage, but he didn’t sacrifice any production on defense. It was arguably McDaniels’ best season as a pro, and it led to his second straight top 100 season in 9-cat leagues.
changed: Minnesota made some moves this offseason, shipping out Julius Randle and Naz Reid while adding LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga. McDaniels’ defense is too important to this team, so his spot in the rotation shouldn’t be impacted. Ball’s addition to the rota- tion will provide a level of playmaking that the Timberwolves haven’t had in a long time.
outlook: For the first time in his career, McDaniels shot over 40 percent from beyond the arc last season. Assuming that doesn’t completely drop off (we can assume there will be a little regression), McDaniels will be the perfect wing alongside LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards. Reports indicated Kuminga will start alongside McDaniels at the forward spots, but that isn’t guaranteed to continue all season. Regardless, McDaniels should still see a similar workload to what he saw last season, and his defense is too valuable for him to see his minutes decrease.

recap: During his first season with Toronto, CMB’s role wasn’t con- sistently large, but he was able to make a big impact during his time on the floor. There were questions about his jumpshot entering the year, and while he wasn’t a high-volume shooter, CMB did knock down 17 triples after hitting nine total in two seasons at South Carolina. When he got the opportunity, he was able to stuff the stat sheet.
changed: Toronto made a swing this summer by adding Kawhi Leonard, and they also added Allen Graves in the draft. Graves isn’t the exact same player, but he fits the same mold that CMB and Scottie Barnes in that they’re all analytics darlings. Sandro Mamukelashvili also left for the Lakers, which should leave the backup center minutes for CMB.
outlook: CMB’s role should be larger in year two, but there will still be a ceiling on his production as a reserve. However, his game is built for him to rack up stats for fantasy managers in limited action. His defensive prowess is the main reason he was drafted in the top 10 in 2025, and it should be valuable for Toronto this season. Assuming that gets him on the floor more, he has a chance to be a strong option for fantasy managers as a bench player, and if any circumstances lead to him entering the starting unit, he’ll become a fantasy star instantly.

recap: Dybantsa was considered by some outlets to be the best high school prospect in the 2025 high school class, and he showcased why during his lone season at BYU. He was a first team All-American, and he led the nation in scoring. Despite Dybantsa scoring 35 points, BYU ended up losing in the first round of the NCAA Tournament. However, he was still one of the best freshmen in recent history.
changed: The Wizards were impressed enough by Dybantsa to select him with the top pick in the draft. He goes from being the best player on BYU to joining a stacked roster, featuring Anthony Davis, Trae Young, Alex Sarr and other exciting young pieces.
outlook: Despite all the talent on the roster, Dybantsa is now the face of the franchise. Even with all the other talent on the roster, the team is be- ing built around him. However, that doesn’t mean he’s the best player on the team, and with AD and Trae on the roster, Washington will be looking to return to the playoffs. Dybantsa should be featured heavily, but things won’t run through him quite yet. He should be among the rookie scoring leaders, but he’ll also have to share touches with some former All-NBA players.

recap: As a top five prospect in the recruiting class, Wilson was one of the best freshmen in college basketball last season. He made the All- ACC first team and All-American second team while also receiving numer- ous other awards. Unfortunately, he suffered a broken thumb on his shoot- ing hand in March, which ended his season before the postseason began.
changed: Wilson was selected by the Bulls with the No. 4 overall pick in June. He shined during summer league, averaging 21.8 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals, 2.5 blocks and 3.3 triples per game. Af- ter only hitting seven three-pointers in 24 games for North Carolina, he knocked down 13 of them in four summer league games.
outlook: Chicago has some young pieces to build with and around, though Wilson has to be considered the one with the most upside. The Bulls don’t have the firepower to compete for a championship, but there are some exciting pieces on the team. Wilson should start from day one, and this team should play at a fast pace, which will play to Wilson’s strengths. He may not be the favorite for Rookie of the Year, but he should make a strong case for the All-Rookie first team and be one of the best rookies in fantasy basketball.

recap: The year got off to a shaky start under new head coach Mike Brown, who decided to bring Hart off the bench to start the year. However, he returned to the starting unit about a month into the season, but Brown was more intentional about not overusing his starters than former head coach Tom Thibodeau was. As a result, Hart played 7.4 fewer minutes per game, which translated to a worse statistical season for Hart.
changed: For the most part, the Knicks are running it back with the same squad after winning the championship. Hart will continue to start and play a pivotal role next season, with the main roster change being that Mitchell Robinson has been replaced with Andre Drummond.
outlook: The Knicks starters played significantly smaller roles last sea- son, which kept them fresh for the playoffs. The change paid off, so it’s unlikely that they do anything differently next season. Hart can provide value in a variety of categories, but not playing the entirety of every game reduces his impact. Still, Hart should be a reliable target in the middle rounds of drafts, as long as you aren’t relying on him for big scoring nights.

recap: Buzelis became a full-time starter in his second season with Chicago, and his numbers took a big leap with the role change. He was one of four players to average at least 1.5 triples and 1.5 blocks per game, joining Victor Wembanyama, Myles Turner and Jay Huff. That jump allowed him to finish in the top 75 in 9-cat leagues at only 21 years old.
changed: Chicago hired Tiago Splitter to be their new head coach after he was the interim for the Trail Blazers for most of last season. The Bulls also added more talent on the wing, signing Norman Powell to a two-year deal and drafting Caleb Wilson and Dailyn Swain.
outlook: The expectations for Buzelis to take another leap in his third season are high. He still has plenty of room to grow, and his minutes could increase again this season, which would be his clearest path to im- provement in fantasy basketball. While he could simply take another step forward, that is a risky bet to make, especially with more scoring talent around him. Success as a shot blocker may result in him finishing high in category leagues once again, but he may not take massive strides forward in other areas.

recap: In his final season as a Charlotte Hornet, the veteran forward played another important role for a Hornets team that came within one win of making the NBA playoffs. Bridges’ counting stats weren’t as great as they had been over the previous three years, missing the 20-point-per- game club for the first time since the 2020-21 season while also posting lower rebound and assist averages since that same season. However, his shooting efficiency crept back up over the 77 regular-season games.
changed: The athletic forward was traded to the Phoenix Suns over the offseason in a deal that sent Grayson Allen and Royce O’Ne- ale to Charlotte. In theory, he seems like a lock to start at forward along- side the talented scoring backcourt of Devin Booker and Jalen Green.
outlook: The Suns’ lack of a true playmaking point guard is foreign ter- ritory for Bridges, who got to play with LaMelo Ball for many years. But that should take away from his motor and knack for playing physically. The re- bounding and three-point shooting, and even if the production isn’t what it was in Charlotte, Bridges should still have value as a likely middle-round pick in fantasy drafts.

recap: For the first time in his career, Murray was hit hard by the injury bug. So much so that he was limited to 23 regular season games, logging his final appearance in late February against the Houston Rock- ets. Presumably, the injuries played a large factor in Murray’s career worst shooting efficiency — 42.0 percent from the field and 27.7 percent from beyond the arc. His rebounding also saw some slippage despite averaging more minutes per game than the previous season.
changed: The Kings are continuing to retool. And with a couple veteran starters from last year’s roster now elsewhere, the focus seems to be on Murray and rookie Darius Acuff Jr. as Sacramento’s players to build around going forward.
outlook: Murray has typically fit in well as a 3-and-D wing along other star players. But given the current roster construction, he’ll be in a good position to step in as the team’s primary scoring option on the offensive end. However, the potential role upgrade will come off a season in which Murray hardly played. He should see a big boost in fantasy production if he can stay on the court.

recap: Collins’ performance during the 2024-25 season was a bit dis- appointing. The minutes, FT% and blocked shots were the second-fewest of his career, and the points were his third-fewest. He also posted a ca- reer-low rebound total. Though the stats were depressed, Collins encour- agingly played in 69 games after logging only 40 appearances the season prior with Utah.
changed: After spending the first six years of his career with the Hawks, Collins will play for his third team in four seasons. He signed a three-year, $51 million deal with the Pistons in the offseason.
outlook: Collins finished outside the top 125 in fantasy hoops for the first time in his career, but he should enjoy new opportunities in Detroit that should lead to a bounceback campaign. The big man is a career 36.9% three-point shooter, and the Pistons love to spread the floor around Cade Cunningham. Collins can play the four, but he’s also capable of running as a small-ball center, which opens the door for in- creased run. Scottie Barnes Photo by John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images

recap: Thompson finished as a top 100 fantasy option for the first time in his career, logging career highs in minutes, games played, assists and steals. His lackluster counting stats were heavily buoyed by his elite defensive contributions, as he was one of only two players (Dyson Dan- iels) to average at least two steals and play at least 40 games.
changed: Thompson will be back for a fourth season in De- troit to run it back with a team that finished as the Eastern Conference’s No. 1 team. The Pistons lost Tobias Harris and added John Collins at the four, and Isaiah Joe was brought in for his three-and-D skills.
outlook: Despite starting all 73 games he played last season, Thomp- son only logged 26 minutes per night. He’s an excellent defender, but he can’t shoot particularly well from anywhere on the floor, and he’s a liabil- ity at the free throw line. The Pistons have emphasized putting shooters around Cade Cunningham, and guys like Duncan Robinson, Kevin Huerter and the aforementioned Joe will eat into Thompson’s playing time be- cause of their outside shots. Thompson’s 2026-27 outlook is unchanged. He’s a fringe 12-team option whose primary value is a steals specialist.

recap: Strictly looking at averages, Watson made a huge leap in his fourth NBA season. He averaged double-digit points for the first time in his career, and set career bests in rebounds, assists, and three-pointers per game, as well. The only thing seeming to not break in Watson’s favor was injury luck; he played in only 54 games last season and finished the season in street clothes.
changed: Watson was a widely sought after restricted free agent this summer. His improvements on the offensive end, paired with his size, athleticism, and youth, ultimately was valued enough by the Cleve- land Cavaliers for them to offer up draft assets to obtain him via trade, and then provide him with a nice pay increase. Watson now goes from a Western Conference contender to an Eastern Conference one, where his role should be larger and more consistent.
outlook: The relocation to Cleveland, and the new contract doesn’t guarantee a breakout season for Watson, who will be playing alongside several other proven all-star players. But given the gravity his teammates garner, he should be able to fit in seamlessly and continue to build on a strong 2025-26 season. He’ll need to first keep his body healthy.

recap: After a solid rookie season, George got off to a strong start in year two. Unfortunately, he didn’t play after March 2, and in the weeks leading up to that date, his minutes were severely limited in order to max- imize Washington’s lottery odds. Missing the fantasy playoffs reduced his impact, but he still showcased significant growth in his second season in the leagues and solidified his spot as an integral piece of the Wizards’ future.
changed: The losing paid off, as Washington lucked into the top pick in the draft, which allowed them to select AJ Dybantsa. Trae Young and Anthony Davis are also in town, with Trae playing in a handful of games last season, while AD hasn’t debuted yet.
outlook: While George should still be a starter for the Wizards along- side Trae, Dybantsa, AD and Alex Sarr, his role will be dramatically different from last season. Thankfully, George has been able to make an impact in a variety of ways, so he should still be valuable for fantasy managers mov- ing forward. He should still be able to provide defensive stats and triples, but his assists should drop off with the ball in his hands less. However, with Trae setting him up, he may improve his shooting percentage and reduce his turnovers.

recap: Jabari Smith Jr. posted a number of career highs in 2025-26, including points, assists, steals, blocked shots and three-pointers. He finished the season as a top 100 fantasy option for the first time in his four-year NBA career. Smith Jr. posted 16 double-doubles for the second straight campaign, and he appeared in at least 76 games for the third time. Houston’s young PF scored 20+ points 19 times and dropped 30+ twice.
changed: The Rockets enjoyed a relatively quiet offseason, and the roster looks similar to the one from 2025-26.
outlook: Through four seasons, fantasy managers know what they’re getting with JSJ. He’s a stretch four who lives outside the arc, posts mod- erate rebound totals, doesn’t get teammates involved too effectively and shoots with moderate efficiency. A top 100 finish is certainly within the realm of possibility, but that likely represents his ceiling, making him a later-round selection in 12-team leagues.

recap: In his first full season in Miami, Wiggins put together a solid year that featured new career highs for three-point percentage and free throw percentage, and it was also the first time he averaged at least one steal and one block per game for a full season in his career. That allowed him to return top 75 value over the course of the season, though his scor- ing average dropped off from the previous season.
changed: The Heat roster will look a bit different next sea- son with Giannis Antetokounmpo in town. Wiggins will still be part of the starting unit, and this roster currently lacks depth, meaning he may end up seeing his minutes rise.
outlook: Wiggins is a solid producer, but he doesn’t truly excel in any individual category. That limits his upside, but he’s a safe option to take in the middle-to-late rounds. His improved shooting efficiency last season helped his value in category leagues, but that has always been a weak- ness for him. Wiggins is a high-floor, low-ceiling option, meaning you shouldn’t ever reach for him.

recap: Camara was one of 18 players to appear in all 82 games last season, and he’s now played 70+ games in all three seasons in the league. His playing time, points, assists and triples increased for the second straight season, and he finished inside the top 125 for the second straight campaign. The Dayton product started every one of Portland’s games in 2025-26.
changed: The Trail Blazers will welcome Damian Lillard back from a season lost recovering from a torn left Achilles, and Lillard will be joined by Ja Morant in a new-look Portland backcourt.
outlook: The Blazers may be deeper at guard, but the depth chart hasn’t changed much at forward, and Camara is projected to open the season as a starter alongside Deni Avdija, Donovan Clingan and the afore- mentioned backcourt of Lillard and Morant. Camara offers 3-and-D value as a late-round add in 12-team leagues for his steals and triples, but fan- tasy managers shouldn’t expect him to crack the top 100 due to his lack of meaningful production across other categories.

recap: Despite a number of key injuries in the frontcourt, Washing- ton’s second full season in Dallas saw dips in minutes, points, rebounds, assists, steals, three-pointers, FG% and FT%. Availability was a concern once again, and Washington has missed a combined 51 games across the last two seasons. For the fifth time in seven seasons, the Kentucky product failed to crack the top 100 in per-game fantasy value. Kevin Durant Photo by Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images
changed: Kyrie Irving will return from a torn left ACL that sidelined him for the entirety of the 2025-26 season, and Dereck Lively II is nearing a return from right foot surgery. The Mavericks took forward Morez Johnson Jr. with the ninth pick in the draft, and they added Santi Aldama and Zaccharie Risacher.
outlook: Washington’s downward trend in production could continue into the 2026-27 campaign, as there are suddenly more mouths to feed, particularly at forward. Washington has value as a three-and-D specialist, but fantasy managers should temper expectations about his scoring and rebounding. He’s more of a late-round flier playing on a crowded roster.

recap: Mamu posted career highs across the board in 2025-26, fin- ishing the season inside the top 300 in per-game fantasy value for the first time in his five-year career. He split time with Collin Murray-Boyles at center filling in for the injured Jakob Poeltl, and Manu made the most of his opportunities, racking up a career-high four double-doubles and starting 13 games.
changed: Mamukelashvili will play for the new-look Lakers in 2026-27, hoping to secure a regular spot in the frontcourt rotation be- hind Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler.
outlook: The journeyman big will play for his third team in as many years, but he could see minutes in the high teens to low 20s due to the departures of LeBron James and Rui Hachimura. He was a top 175 guy in 2025-26 with just 21.9 minutes per game, so he has standalone value in deeper leagues. At best, he’s a late-round dart throw in 12-team leagues, but he would be a strong waiver wire add if Walker Kessler was forced to miss time.

recap: DeRozan averaged fewer than 20 points per game for the first time in 13 seasons and grabbed fewer than three rebounds for the first time since his rookie campaign. His 4.1 assists were his fewest in nine sea- sons. Despite the step back in counting stats, DeRozan offered his usual high-efficiency/low-turnover performance that gave him a 14th straight top 100 fantasy finish.
changed: The longtime vet will play for his fifth team in 18 seasons as he joins Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets to fill the void left by Peyton Watson.
outlook: The 37-year-old clearly still has some gas left in the tank, but points, rebounds and assists will be a bit tougher to come by in Denver than they were in Sacramento as he assimilates to life in the Mile High City alongside Jokic, Jamal Murray, Aaron Gordon, Cam Johnson and Chris- tian Braun. A starting gig is not guaranteed, so fantasy managers should temper expectations. Still, given his history of consistency, durability and efficiency, the midrange merchant is a safe, late-round fantasy selection.

recap: Jokic has been so consistently excellent that incredible numbers simply seem commonplace. Over the last six seasons, the Joker has won three MVPs and been runner up three times. In that six- game stretch, Jokic averaged 26.9 points, 12.4 rebounds, 9.3 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.8 blocks and 1.3 triples while shooting 58.3% from the floor and 82.4% from the charity stripe. Jokic has averaged a triple-double in each of the last two seasons, and in 2025-26, he became the first player in league history to lead the league in rebounds and assists in the same campaign.
changed: The Nuggets lost Peyton Watson and added De- Mar DeRozan, but DeRozan won’t eat into Jokic’s production. The big man will be backed up by Marvin Bagley III, but MB3 is simply a depth option and not a threat to steal minutes.
outlook: Jokic appeared in a career-low 65 games last season, which is a testament to his durability. Jokic has appeared in at least 70 games in nine of 11 seasons, playing in 69 and 65 games in the other two. Jokic has been a first-round fantasy option in eight straight seasons. Over the last five seasons, he’s got four No. 1 finishes and one No. 2 finish. Joker’s only serious competition for fantasy’s top spot is Victor Wembanyama, but Wemby has missed 54 games over the last two seasons. Managers with the first pick in their drafts should weigh Jokic’s consistency and availabil- ity against Wemby’s ceiling and risk for injury.

recap: After three phenomenal seasons in the NBA, it’s safe to say Wemby is already living up to his pre-draft hype. The “Extraterrestrial” recorded career highs in points and rebounds, and he led the league in blocks for a third straight campaign. Wembanyama shot better than 50% for the first time in his career and he got to the charity stripe a career-high seven times a night, focusing more on attacking the paint than shooting three-pointers. He won Defensive Player of the Year and was an MVP final- ist as he guided San Antonio to the Finals following a six-season playoff drought.
changed: The Spurs added Tobias Harris in free agency, but otherwise, they’ll run it back with essentially the same lineup that came up short in the NBA Finals to the Knicks.
outlook: Wembanyama has finished no worse than sixth in per-game 8-cat value since entering the league, and he’s been fantasy’s No. 2 player in each of the last two seasons. His unique ability to score, rebound, hit threes and rack up defensive stats at an otherworldly level gives him a sturdy floor and a monstrous ceiling. He made improvements in efficiency and turnovers in Year 3, and incremental improvements in Year 4 could be enough for him to overtake Nikola Jokic as fantasy’s Numero Uno. The sky’s the limit for Wemby who will be off the board first or second in 2026- 27 fantasy basketball drafts.

recap: For the ninth time in 11 seasons, Towns finished as a sec- ond-rounder in fantasy hoops. KAT averaged fewer than 10 rebounds in each of his final three seasons with the Timberwolves, but he’s averaged at least 11.9 rebounds in each of his two seasons with the Knicks. Towns’ scoring and rebounding took a backseat in the playoffs, as he excelled as a playmaker and defender to help guide the Knicks to their first title in 53 years.
changed: Towns will be backed up by Andre Drummond, rather than Mitchell Robinson after the latter signed with Boston in the offseason. Like Robinson, Drummond is a capable veteran backup, but Towns is the go-to guy at center, and his role likely won’t change in Year 3 with the franchise.
outlook: Towns has seven top 10 fantasy seasons under his belt, in- cluding one in his first year with the Knicks. His upside is tremendous, and with only one season outside the top 25, he’s been the model of consisten- cy throughout his career. Towns is an elite rebounder, strong scorer and capable facilitator who knocks down enough three-pointers and posts enough defensive stats to offer a reliable floor. His playing time cooled off in his first season with Mike Brown at the helm, but Towns’ minutes and production should be enough to pay off his mid-second-round asking price.

recap: Sengun enjoyed the best fantasy finish of his career behind strong production in a few categories. His rebounds were the second-low- est mark of his career, but his points were the second-most, and he of- fered career-best marks in assists, steals, blocks, three-pointers and min- utes played. He finished behind only Nikola Jokic for most triple-doubles by a center with four.
changed: Houston made no significant offseason moves. The return of Fred VanVleet may mean less playmaking responsibilities for the big man, but FVV’s availability shouldn’t cut into Sengun’s assist numbers too much.
outlook: The playmaking center finished 34th in per-game fantasy value thanks to solid contributions as a scorer, rebounder, facilitator and defender. His fantasy value could rise to new heights if he develops an outside shot and improves his efficiency from the charity stripe, and he still has room to grow as a facilitator. Sengun has a reliable floor with a massive ceiling if he can continue to develop and improve in Year 6.

recap: Sabonis has been a durable option throughout his career, but injuries limited him to just 19 games in 2025-26. He still offered enough production to finish as a top 75 fantasy option, but his counting stats and efficiency took a nosedive. The playmaking big failed to record a tri- ple-double after totaling 50 across his last three seasons.
changed: Sabonis’ extended absences allowed rookie Max- ime Raynaud to take on meaningful minutes immediately and expedite his development. Fellow rookie Dylan Cardwell enjoyed similar opportunities, and both backup bigs averaged 20+ minutes per game in 2025-26.
outlook: After finishing with the NBA’s worst record and selecting PG of the future Darius Acuff with the No. 7 pick, the Kings could be looking to the future rather than focusing on wins in 2026-27. Sabonis and Zach LaVine could end up on new teams sooner rather than later as Sacramen- to looks to accelerate its rebuild. Sabonis has tremendous upside as a big man who can rack up rebounds and assists in bunches, so as long as he’s healthy, he should be a valuable fantasy contributor, no matter where he’s playing.

recap: Adebayo finished as a top 55 fantasy option for the seventh straight season, averaging at least 20 points and 10 rebounds for the first time in his career. He offered useful assists and defensive stats and even added a three-point shot to his game. His 2025-26 season will, however, be remembered for his stunning, 83-point eruption against the Wizards on March 10, that moved him into second place on the NBA’s single-game scoring leaderboard ahead of Kobe Bryant and behind only Wilt Cham- berlain.
changed: Miami gutted its depth to acquire Giannis Ante- tokounmpo, and the Bucks included Bobby Portis in that deal. The Heat added Tim Hardaway Jr., Klay Thompson and Nick Richards to bolster the team’s depth.
outlook: Adebayo will face obvious competition for touches from An- tetokounmpo, but aside from the superstar, Miami’s roster is weaker from top to bottom than it was a season ago. Adebayo could see an uptick in scoring counting stats, particularly as a facilitator, and he could enjoy eas- ier scoring opportunities playing alongside the Greek Freak and a number of capable three-point shooters.

recap: Kessler’s fourth season was one to forget, as he was lim- ited to just five games due to shoulder surgery. It was a disappointing campaign for the seven-footer, who posted career highs in points (11.1), rebounds (12.2), assists (1.7) and blocks (2.4) the season prior. Though it was a small sample size, Kessler topped his points and assists in his five healthy games and flashed upside as a playmaker (3 APG) and three-point shooter (1.2 3PM).
changed: Kessler was traded to the Lakers in the offseason, and he inked a four-year, $130 million contract to join Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic as franchise cornerstones for the foreseeable future.
outlook: Kessler is an interesting fantasy option for the 2026-27 cam- paign for a number of reasons. First, he’s been an elite source of tradi- tional big man stats (REB, FG%, BLK) throughout his career, but will he add a consistent three-point game to his repertoire? Next, will he be fully healthy for the start of the season, and how many games will he play? Finally, can he improve on his historically atrocious FT%? There are plenty of question marks, but Kessler has early-round upside as a dominant rim protector and lob threat in a Luka Doncic offense, especially with Dean- dre Ayton gone and lack of quality depth behind him at center. His early fourth-round ADP seems appropriate.

recap: Duren was named an All-Star for the first time as he earned All-NBA Third Team honors behind a career-best season. The 2022 lottery pick posted career-highs in points and steals while averaging a dou- ble-double for the third straight campaign. Duren shot efficiently from the floor and from the charity stripe as he finished with a career-high 6.1 FTA per game. The big man was on his way to a monster contract extension before disappearing in the playoffs with averages of only 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds on 51.4/67.4 shooting splits.
changed: Detroit traded Isaiah Stewart in the offseason, but the team added John Collins, and Paul Reed will be back. Duren will have to contend with the pair for frontcourt touches, and Collins in particular could eat into his playing time due to his ability to stretch the floor.
outlook: It’s anyone’s guess when and how Duren’s contract negotia- tions will wrap up with Detroit, but the lingering talks may have a negative impact on his 2026-27 performance if they continue too much longer. Du- ren is seeking more annually than what the team has offered, but his poor playoff performance doesn’t give him any leverage. The addition of stretch four John Collins, the postseason emergence of Paul Reed and uncertain future with the team are three major red flags. Duren doesn’t shoot threes, and he doesn’t rack up defensive stats at a high level, so the risk of draft- ing him as a mid-round option may be far higher than the reward.

recap: After logging only 19.8 minutes and starting 37 games as a rookie, Clingan broke out in Year 2 as the established starting center. His minutes spiked, and he started all 77 games in which he appeared. The UConn product offered traditional big-man stats but also added a three- point game to his repertoire. Clingan corralled 20+ rebounds twice and finished the campaign with 37 double-doubles. His boost in production was good for fifth-round fantasy value.
changed: Portland’s backcourt will get a new look after add- ing Ja Morant and welcoming Damian Lillard back from injury, but the Blaz- ers didn’t add anyone in the frontcourt to siphon minutes from Clingan.
outlook: The big man has been durable early into his career, appearing in 143 of a possible 164 games. He faces little competition behind him on the depth chart, so fantasy managers should feel confident selecting him in the middle rounds of drafts. Clingan still has room to grow as a scorer, and improved efficiency from the free throw line could improve his fantasy value significantly.

recap: It was business as usual for Embiid in 2025-26, as he dealt with injuries throughout the season and missed more than 41 games for the third straight campaign. When available, he was a productive scorer, but his assist numbers dipped, and his rebounds were the fewest of his career. Managers who were able to stomach his rollercoaster availability got some top 20 performances out of Embiid, but that was the only silver lining to an otherwise-disappointing campaign.
changed: Quite a lot. The Sixers had the busiest offseason of any franchise as they traded Paul George for Jaylen Brown, signed LeB- ron James and added Anfernee Simons, Dean Wade and Kentavious Cald- well-Pope to shore up the bench. Victor Wembanyama Photo by Geoff Burke-Imagn Images
outlook: Embiid has appeared in 96 of a possible 246 games over the last three seasons, so availability will be the biggest concern for the 2023 MVP. As if his injury history wasn’t enough to scare fantasy managers away, he’ll likely see his production take a dip with such a deep and tal- ented roster around him.

recap: Sarr’s minutes were nearly identical in Year 2 to the playing time he received as a rookie, but he improved his shooting percentage from 39.4% to 48.2%, and his scoring jumped from 13 to 16.3 points per game. Sarr also improved his rebounds, assists, steals and FT% on his way to a top 65 fantasy finish.
changed: Sarr underwent surgery on a fractured right foot in June, but he is expected to be ready for the start of the season. Injuries notwithstanding, he’ll also face competition for frontcourt minutes from Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton.
outlook: Sarr is a building block for Washington’s future, and he figures to remain a regular part of the rotation, particularly given his defensive acumen and ability to stretch the floor. Still, it would be irresponsible not to expect a dip in counting stats given the new frontcourt teammates and the additions of Trae Young and No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa. Sarr’s early ADP is in the sixth round, and that feels a bit rich considering the aforementioned changes.

recap: Okongwu took a clear step forward over the course of the 2025-26 season. Despite beginning the season as Kristaps Porzingis’ backup at center, Okongwu eventually took over as the team’s full-time start in the middle, and set career-highs in points, assists, steals, and minutes played per game.
changed: Coming off a strong season for the Hawks, the team doesn’t appear to look too much different than it did a season ago. The big offseason splashes came on the perimeter, with the additions of Luguentz Dort (trade), Aaron Wiggins (trade), and Kingston Flemings (draft), which shouldn’t have much of an impact on Okongwu’s production during the 2026-27 season.
outlook: A mid-round draft pick is the likely range for those fantasy managers looking to draft Okongwu. If he can continue to make strides on his three-point shooting, as he did a season ago, while regaining his overall shooting efficiency that escaped him last season, he could poten- tially outperform his value. Expect another strong season from him on both ends of the floor.

recap: Zubac averaged 30+ minutes per game for the first time in his career in 2024-25, and he parlayed that newfound playing time into a career-best season. The Clippers’ big man ended the ‘24-25 campaign just outside the fourth round in per-game fantasy value, but he couldn’t equal that success last season. Injuries limited the usually durable Zubac to only 48 games, and his counting stats and FG% took a dip. He ended the season just outside the top 100.
changed: Zubac was dealt to the Pacers at the trade dead- line for Bennedict Mathurin, Isaiah Jackson, two first-round picks and a second-round pick. He appeared in only five games for his new team and averaged fewer than 25 minutes.
outlook: Zubac has been playing for Croatia during the FIBA World Cup qualifiers, so it’s safe to say he’s good to go for the start of the 2026-27 campaign. Indiana utilized an underwhelming center rotation of Jackson, Jay Huff and others last season, but Zubac will be the unquestioned start- ing center for a team that’s been desperately lacking a consistent option at the position. He could be in line for a strong bounceback effort.

recap: Ware’s minutes remained virtually unchanged in Year 2, though he posted career highs in points, rebounds, steals, blocked shots and three-pointers. Ware started 34 games and posted new single-game highs in points (28) and rebounds (20). He scored 20+ eight times, re- cording a double-double in each of them. The big man backed up Bam Adebayo, but Miami employed the pair together at times in double-big lineups. Ware finished inside the top 100 fantasy options.
changed: Ware was dealt to Milwaukee in the trade that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami, and he’ll enter Year 3 on a new roster.
outlook: Ware will compete for frontcourt minutes with Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma, though given the Bucks’ offseason trade of Giannis An- tetokounmpo, it’s unclear if the pair are in Milwaukee’s long-term plans. The Bucks are entering a rebuild, and they’d be wise to focus on Ware’s development rather than getting more minutes for their veteran players. Ware should see more run in Milwaukee than he did in Miami, and he’s got a chance to end the season as the Bucks’ starting center.

recap: Edey boosted his production in every category except 3PM in Year 2, averaging a double-double, swatting nearly two shots per game and shooting efficiently from the field and from the charity stripe. Unfor- tunately, his productive start was cut short due to an ankle injury that required surgery in March. Edey’s numbers in 11 games would have been good enough for third-round fantasy value.
changed: Edey has some new competition for frontcourt minutes in No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer, and Memphis added Isaiah Stewart and Quinten Post to back him up.
outlook: Edey also had ankle surgery in the summer of 2025, and avail- ability is a major concern following his second operation less than a year later. The big man has appeared in just 77 games across two NBA seasons, and managers drafting him should understand the risk of missed games and fewer minutes with a much deeper frontcourt rotation.

recap: Gobert’s 2025-26 counting stats were identical to his 2024-25 numbers, but he finished outside the top 100 in per-game fantasy value for the first time since his rookie campaign. Gobert’s poor fantasy finish was due in large part to his horrendous FT%, but he was otherwise as consistent as usual, averaging a double-double and at least 1.2 swats for the 10th straight campaign.
changed: The Timberwolves completely reshaped their ros- ter by trading Julius Randle to the Nets and Naz Reid to the Hornets in a four-team deal that brought LaMelo Ball to Minnesota.
outlook: Minnesota also brought in Jonathan Kuminga, but Gobert’s primary competition for frontcourt minutes is now only Joan Beringer. With Randle and Reid off to new locales and a true PG running the show in Minnesota, Gobert may see more scoring opportunities, and he could be leaned on more heavily for rebounds and blocked shots. He’s in a great position to break back into the top 100, and managers drafting the veteran center would be smart to consider a punt-FT% build.

recap: Allen was as steady as always during his 56 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 season. He remained an efficient scorer, was good on the glass, and was productive on the defensive end of the floor. The injuries were the main reason he didn’t finish higher in fantasy leagues — his 26 missed games tied a career high.
changed: Fortunately for Allen, not a lot has changed in terms of Cleveland’s roster construction. He’ll benefit from a full training camp and more reps with James Harden, who wasn’t part of the Cavaliers until last season’s trade deadline. Their partnership as a pick-and-roll duo should be beneficial to Allen’s scoring and efficiency.
outlook: Allen’s not going to shoot three-pointers and isn’t much of a playmaker with the ball in his hands — those limitations take away from his value in fantasy basketball leagues. But for a fantasy manager who may be in pursuit of high field-goal percentages, rebounding and stocks, Allen is a reliable option who shouldn’t go too high in drafts.

recap: Sharpe’s fifth season saw him post career highs in games played, minutes, points, rebounds, assists, steals and FG% while operat- ing primarily as Nic Claxton’s backup. He posted solid numbers in seven starts and finished the campaign with eight double-digit rebound games and 21 games with at least one block.
changed: Nic Claxton was dealt to the Bulls in a four-team deal that sent Julius Randle to Brooklyn, Naz Reid to Charlotte and LaMelo Ball to Minnesota.
outlook: With Claxton gone, Sharpe should open the season as the Nets’ starting center. In 21 career starts, Sharpe has averaged 11.2 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 0.8 steals and a block across 24.6 minutes. His early ADP is in the 10th round, making him an intriguing value play for fantasy managers who wait to take centers later in drafts.

recap: Despite multiple injuries across the Bucks’ roster in 2025- 26, Turner saw a reduction in playing time and counting stats. His min- utes, points and blocks were his fewest since his rookie campaign, and Turner posted career-lows in rebounds and FG%. A model of consistency throughout his career, Turner finished outside the top 100 in fantasy for only the second time in his career and the first since his first year in the league.
changed: The Bucks kicked off their rebuild by trading Gi- annis Antetokounmpo to the Heat for Kel’el Ware, Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis and multiple picks.
outlook: Turner will face new competition at center in Ware, but that will be if he remains on the roster. The veteran big man is a trade candi- date as Milwaukee looks to develop its young core. A three-and-D special- ist, Turner will likely have substantial fantasy value no matter where he lands, but fit and surrounding roster will factor into that equation.

recap: Injuries hampered Hartenstein in 2025-26 following a ca- reer-best first-season in OKC. He played in just 47 of the 82 regular-season games for the Thunder and sacrificed some minutes on a per-game basis. As a result, his fantasy value fell, even with his skill set and on-court con- tributions being similar to the prior season whenever he was available and on the floor.
changed: Even with the Thunder spending an early draft pick on Aday Mara to add value to their frontcourt, Hartenstein should feel safe in his role. Oklahoma City showed their commitment to Hartenstein by re-signing him to a 3-year, $75 million contract extension this offsea- son, leaving him as the team’s clear starting center ahead of the 2026-27 season.
outlook: Better health would do wonders for Hartenstein from a fanta- sy basketball perspective. Assuming he’s the nightly double-double threat with high playmaking upside that he’s been so far during his two seasons with the Thunder, he’ll scratch many itches for those fantasy managers in need of a reliable center. He should be available in the later rounds of drafts.

recap: Injuries limited Poeltl again in the 2025-26 season. For a third straight season, he was unable to make it to the 60-game mark, this time only being around for 46 of the 82 regular-season games. Even when healthy, his production dipped. The veteran center was far less involved in the offense, and fewer minutes led to declines in rebounds, steals, and blocks.
changed: Poeltl’s lack of availability last season led to more opportunities for Collin Murray-Boyles and others to fill in at center. Aside from adding Allen Graves in the draft, the Raptors didn’t make any big splashes this offseason when it comes to the frontcourt. Even the block- buster trade to acquire Kawhi Leonard isn’t likely to change Poeltl’s im- pact much.
outlook: Poor injury luck and a Year 2 jump from Murray-Boyles may be the only things threatening to block production from Poeltl during the 2026-27 season. His noted decrease in scoring and rebounding last sea- son shouldn’t be easily dismissed. However, Toronto doesn’t have much size at the center position, making Poeltl very valuable for the Raptors, even if that value across fantasy basketball leagues isn’t shared.

recap: Following a run as one of the top centers in fantasy basketball, Claxton put together back-to-back rough seasons. He showed tremendous growth as a passer, but he struggled in basically every other facet of his game. It was a season to forget for both Claxton and the Nets.
changed: Claxton gets a fresh start in Chicago and should fill in as the team’s starting center. He’ll go from a bottom-feeding team to one that will be competing for a play-in spot and plays at a much faster pace. Josh Giddey will be feeding Claxton buckets down low, and with Jalen Smith and Zach Collins behind him, Claxton should play a significant role.
outlook: In the past, Claxton has been at his most productive on good teams. He produced second-round value when he was playing alongside Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving for the first half of the season and next to Mikal Bridges and Cameron Johnson for the second half. This Bulls team should be better than the Nets have been in each of the last two seasons, and it wouldn’t be surprising if he returned to producing top 100 value in category formats as one of the league’s premier shot blockers.

recap: In his third season with Boston, Queta saw a major boost in playing time and ran with his new opportunities, posting career-highs in minutes, games played and all counting stats. A depth option for the first four years of his career between the Celtics and Kings, Queta started ev- ery regular-season game in which he appeared. He finished inside the top 275 in fantasy for the first time in his career, ending the season 96th in per-game value.
changed: Queta faced little competition for playing time in Boston’s frontcourt last season, but that will change in 2026-27 with Jayson Tatum back and Mitchell Robinson signed to a three-year deal.
outlook: It’s unclear how Boston’s center rotation will shake out, but Robinson’s new, three-year deal suggests he’ll play a prominent role right out of the gate. Queta’s fantasy value was largely derived from his unques- tioned position atop the depth chart, but with Robinson in the fold, he’ll be splitting minutes at minimum. Queta can be left undrafted outside of deep leagues.

recap: As has been the case throughout his career, injuries were problematic for the veteran center during the 2025-26 season. Porzingis was limited to only 32 regular-season games as he split time with the At- lanta Hawks and Golden State Warriors. His stats were nearly identical at both stops, with slight regression in shooting efficiency coming during his 15 appearances with Golden State.
changed: The former NBA champion re-signed with the War- riors over the offseason and will get re-integrated into a veteran nucleus that he played well with to end the season. Aside from the drafting Yaxel Lendenborg, who will log some minutes at forward, there weren’t any outside additions to the frontcourt; certainly not any that would remotely jeopardize Porzingis’ role in the nightly rotation.
outlook: Can he stay healthy? Unfortunately, there hasn’t been any ev- idence in recent years to suggest Porzingis will be on the floor much. For that reason, it’s hard to place much fantasy value on even an incredibly unique and versatile 7-footer who can thrive from beyond the arc on one end of the floor while being a legitimate shot blocker on the other. He’ll be a nice contributor for the Warriors when healthy.

recap: It was an up-and-down season for Nurkić, but when he was on the floor consistently, he was able to turn in production in ways that he hasn’t been able to in recent years. This was his first season in Utah, and he quickly secured the starting job after Walker Kessler went down for the year. Nurkić ended up having a solid stretch from late December to late January, which included a stretch of three straight triple-doubles.
changed: Kessler is now a Laker, which means Nurkić is the team’s starting center, and they’ll be trying to push for the postseason. Nurkić shouldn’t miss two months of games due to a nose injury this year. Plus, with Jaren Jackson Jr. next time, Nurkić should be the team’s leading rebounder.
outlook: Nurkić hasn’t been a coveted option entering fantasy drafts over the last two seasons, but there is some real intrigue here. He isn’t the dominant fantasy option he was in Portland, but the Jazz desperately need him to control the glass and paint if they want to be competitive in the West. Nurkić should play a significant role as the starting center in Utah, which could lead to some strong production for fantasy managers, specifically in rebounds, assists and defensive stats.

recap: The big man out of Duke had a muted impact in his rook- ie campaign, averaging 3.0 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.7 blocked shots across 8.9 minutes in 46 appearances. He flashed tremendous upside when given additional opportunities, averaging 11 points, 14 rebounds and 2.5 blocks in two games in which he played 25+ minutes. He finished with per-36 averages of 12.2 points, 11.6 rebounds and 2.9 swats.
changed: Mark Williams underwent shoulder surgery on September 10, which opens up the starting center job in Phoenix.
outlook: Maluach will compete with Oso Ighodaro for the vacant gig at center, but the former could have the inside track after a strong showing at Summer League. Maluach averaged 19.5 points, 1.3 steals, 2.0 blocks and a league-best 12.8 rebounds in four appearances. He’s an interesting late-round sleeper with top 100 upside.

recap: Robinson once again came off the bench and played a key re- serve role behind Karl-Anthony Towns as a rebounder and rim protector. Though his playing time was limited, Robinson was ultra efficient when on the court, averaging 10.4 points, 16.1 rebounds and 3.8 “stocks” per-36 min- utes.
