changed: After eight years in New York and a 2026 NBA championship, Robinson left the Knicks in the offseason and signed a three-year, $47.4 million deal with the Celtics.
outlook: Robinson will have to compete with Neemias Queta (who had a career year in 2025-26), but the former’s new deal suggests he has the inside track to earn the starting gig. Robinson logged fewer than 20 min- utes per game in each of the last two seasons after Karl-Anthony Towns joined the Knicks, but he’s set for an uptick in playing time with his new team. Given Robinson’s per-minute efficiency and the prospect of a fea- tured role, he’s a sneaky later-round fantasy selection.

recap: Diabate saw the most minutes of his career in 2025-26, and he turned his increased playing time into new career highs in every measur- able fantasy category. He started the season on the bench but eventually wrestled the starting center job from rookie Ryan Kalkbrenner and started 49 of 73 appearances.
changed: Charlotte’s frontcourt rotation will now feature Kalkbrenner, Naz Reid and rookie first-rounder Hannes Steinbach.
outlook: Diabate and Kalkbrenner cannibalized each other’s produc- tion in 2025-26, and cannibalization should be even more prevalent in the upcoming season due to the number of new additions to the frontcourt. Outside of Naz Reid, fantasy managers should take a “wait-and-see” ap- proach with Steinbach, Kalkbrenner and Diabate.

recap: After seven seasons with the Bucks, the veteran big man signed with the Clippers and started the season as the backup center behind Ivica Zubac. The latter got injured, and Lopez started the final 34 games of the season, seeing a slight uptick in production. He was a bor- derline 12-team option after joining the first unit, finishing 128th in per- game fantasy value over the final two months of the season.
changed: The Clippers picked up Lopez’s team option for the 2026-27 season, and with Zubac traded to the Pacers, Lopez could open the season as the starting center.
outlook: Lopez will turn 39 during his 19th season, and it’s fair to won- der how much gas he has left in the tank. The Kawhi Leonard era ended with a whimper and a bang as the two-time champ and Defensive Player of the Year was dealt to the Raptors, and the league levied monster sanc- tions against the Clippers for circumventing the salary cap. Los Angeles also traded James Harden and let Bennedict Mathurin walk in the offsea- son, leaving LA’s roster gutted. BroLo isn’t the team’s center of the future, but he should play a featured role in the frontcourt out of pure necessity, making him worth a look in the last round of fantasy drafts.

recap: In his second year with the Pistons, “Bball Paul” served as a depth option again, but his playing time and production saw a slight up- tick. He was a strong streamer when called upon to start, and he averaged a healthy 15.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.9 steals, 2.0 blocks and 0.5 triples across 11 games with the first unit.
changed: The Pistons traded Isaiah Stewart to the Grizzlies for three second-round picks, and Stewart should slot in as the top backup center to Jalen Duren.
outlook: Duren has been engaged in contract extension talks with the Pistons for quite some time, and it’s unclear when/if that deal will get done and how the ongoing negotiations will impact Duren’s playing time or production. Reed played well off the bench as a complimentary option to the struggling Duren in the Eastern Conference semifinals against the Cavs, and his work as a starter speaks for itself. He’s an intriguing late- round dart throw in 12-team leagues.

recap: Carter Jr. has been a solid fantasy option for a while, though his production has ticked down in recent years. However, he set a new career high for games played and saw one of the highest minutes allo- cations of his career. He’s not as productive as he was five years ago, but WCJ was a reliable, effective option as the starting center in Orlando last season.
changed: Moritz Wagner is gone, but Nikola Vucevic, who the Magic sent to Chicago in the deal that landed them WCJ years ago, is back. Vucevic will likely slot in as WCJ’s backup, with Goga Bitadze as the third option. They also have a new head coach in Sean Sweeney.
outlook: Though his minutes may go back down with Vucevic in town, WCJ is still the starting center for the Magic. He’ll continue to contribute decent value across the board without dominating any individual cate- gory. Even in a smaller role, WCJ could see his numbers bump up slightly under Sweeney, assuming he’s able to maximize this roster. However, it is unlikely that he improves enough to become a must-roster player, and there isn’t enough upside to take him as a late-round swing.

recap: Raynaud slipped to the second round of the draft last summer, but he ended up being the only non-lottery pick to make an All-Rookie team. With Domantas Sabonis injured, he stepped into a significant role for the Kings and was an impactful fantasy player down the stretch. He was one of the few bright spots in what was a disastrous season for Sac- ramento.
changed: Sacramento’s squad is healthier entering the sea- son, but there is still some uncertainty as to whether Sabonis will remain with the team for the year or end up being traded. Raynaud should be the backup center to start the year after finishing last season as the starter.
outlook: While Raynaud was a fifth-round producer in category leagues during the final two months of last season, the path to him being a productive option isn’t guaranteed. Last year, he benefited from injuries ahead of him on the depth chart, and it will likely take a similar scenario, or a trade, for him to step into big minutes. He shouldn’t be considered a valuable target in drafts, but he will be a must-roster player if something changes with Sabonis’ status.

recap: Steinbach was a one-and-done at Washington who aver- aged 18.5 points, 11.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.1 steals, 1.2 blocks and 0.6 three-pointers. He led D-1 in rebound average and was named to the All-Big Ten team. The highlight of his season came on March 4 when he delivered a 22-point, 24-rebound, two-block performance in a 91-72 win over USC.
changed: Steinbach was the final pick of the 2026 NBA Draft Lottery, as the Hornets took him 14th overall.
outlook: The rookie will compete with Moussa Diabate and sec- ond-year man Ryan Kalkbrenner for the starting center spot, and new- comer Naz Reid could end up seeing some run at center. It’s unclear how the center rotation will shake out in Charlotte, but Steinbach’s upside is capped in this crowded rotation.

recap: Queen burst onto the scene fairly early as a rookie. After get- ting his feet wet in October, he logged several big games in November — one 30-point game, and three others in which he scored at least 20 points. Queen was even better as a scorer in December but couldn’t sus- tain his scoring level at the turn of the calendar year. Yet, the rookie big man showed his well-roundedness as a rebounder and scorer throughout his entire rookie campaign, which was enough to land him a spot on the All-Rookie Second Team.
changed: The Pelicans’ roster won’t look much different than it did a season ago. Zion Williamson will be the focus of the front- court, whether he starts at power forward or center, while the perimeter options consist of the Pelicans’ usual, long-tenured veteran options. How- ever, New Orleans’ hiring of head coach Jamahl Mosley, could change how the Pels operate.
outlook: Going into Year 2, Queen finds himself in a good spot. There are enough frontcourt minutes available for him to earn and make a sec- ond-year leap. Even if he weren’t to make major progress in any areas of his game, simply logging more minutes than the 25.0 that he averaged as a rookie should allow him to see a nice bump in production.

recap: The rookie from France played a limited role in his inaugural campaign, playing third fiddle behind Rudy Gobert and Naz Reid at center. He averaged fewer than eight minutes per game, but when given addition- al opportunities, he shined. In five games with at least 20 minutes played (two starts), Beringer averaged 14 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.4 swats.
changed: Naz Reid and Julius Randle were dealt to the Hor- nets and Nets respectively as part of a four-team deal that sent LaMelo Ball to the Timberwolves.
outlook: Beringer is suddenly the Timberwolves’ top backup center be- hind Gobert, and he should naturally see an uptick in playing time, even as a relief option off the bench. Given his strong performances when provid- ed extra minutes, Beringer is an appealing late-rounder in deep leagues. He would be an instant streamer in 12-team leagues if Gobert was forced to miss time.

recap: Filipowski showcased some growth in his second season, and he put together some monster performances down the stretch of the season, which made him a must-roster player for a time. That came while Utah was more focused on lottery odds and player development than win- ning, but Filipowski proved his ability to stuff the stat sheet in fantasy hoops when he is given the chance.
changed: The only roster change the Jazz made this summer that may impact Filipowski is the addition of Jaxson Hayes. However, the entire mindset of the team has changed. Instead of being a team looking for talent, which would allow Filipowski a couple months of being a start- er, this is a squad with its eyes set on the postseason.
outlook: The time has finally come for Utah to make a push for the postseason. While that isn’t guaranteed, Filipowski’s minutes won’t be pri- oritized if he isn’t helping the team win, and he won’t be a starter if there aren’t injuries in front of him. He can be productive if he gets the opportu- nity, but that isn’t enough for him to be worth drafting. Keep an eye on him during the season, but he shouldn’t be more than a late-round dart throw.

recap: Drummond played his most minutes in four seasons as he played a prominent role in Philadelphia’s frontcourt. With Joel Embiid side- lined for most of the campaign, Drummond averaged 6.4 points and 8.4 rebounds across 19.5 minutes, and he was a reliable streamer in 26 starts.
changed: After two seasons with the 76ers, Drummond signed a one-year, $3.9 million deal to join the New York Knicks, where he’ll back up Karl-Anthony Towns as New York begins its title defense.
outlook: The veteran big man is still a strong source of rebounds and defensive stats on a per-minute basis, and he should see meaningful min- utes in the vacant Mitchell Robinson role. He’s worth a look in deep leagues as a rebounding specialist, and sharp fantasy managers should keep an eye out for Karl-Anthony Towns injuries throughout the season, as Drum- mond will offer streaming appeal when inserted into the starting five.

recap: After a major dip in playing time in 2024-25, Stewart’s minutes got a slight increase, and his production was much improved. The big man was particularly active as a 3-and-D stretch four and small-ball five, rack- ing up a career-high in blocked shots while shooting 33.3% from beyond the arc. For the sixth straight season, he finished outside the top 150 in per-game fantasy value.
changed: Stewart was dealt to the Grizzlies for three sec- ond-round picks after spending the first six seasons of his career with the Pistons.
outlook: The Grizzlies used the No. 3 pick in the draft on Duke standout Cameron Boozer, and Zach Edey could be back to open the season after undergoing ankle surgery in March. If Edey is available, Stewart could be the first big off the bench, but given Edey’s injury history, there is the pos- sibility that he makes some spot starts throughout the season. Stewart is best viewed as a deep-league guy who offers more on the NBA court than he does in fantasy hoops lineups.

recap: Oh, boy. Here we go again. Williams suffered a torn labrum in his left shoulder and underwent surgery on September 10. He’ll miss significant time, adding yet another extended absence to a growing list of injuries. Through four seasons, he’s played in 166 games and missed 162.
changed: Williams will be sidelined for a yet undetermined amount of time to open the 2026-27 campaign.
outlook: Bleak. That’s the easiest way to sum up Williams’ outlook. He’s got the size and skills to be a valuable fantasy center, but he’s rarely avail- able, and managers who draft him are always waiting for the other shoe to drop. He should remain on the waiver wire in redraft fantasy leagues, and he’s becoming quite frustrating for dynasty managers.

recap: Kalkbrenner made a limited impact in his inaugural cam- paign, and his production waned as the season progressed. The big man opened the season as Charlotte’s starting center, but he eventually ceded that job to Moussa Diabate, who enjoyed a career year.
changed: The Hornets received Naz Reid from the Timber- wolves in the LaMelo Ball trade, and they spent the No. 14 pick on Wash- ington big man Hannes Steinbach.
outlook: For years, Charlotte’s Achilles heel was its lack of depth at center, but the team has done a complete 180 in that department as the frontcourt is now wildly crowded. Trusting Kalkbrenner will be tough in Year 2 with additional competition from Reid and Steinbach, and he’s best viewed as a late-round flier in deeper leagues.

recap: After two seasons at UCLA, Mara enjoyed a phenomenal third season when he transferred to Michigan. The big man earned All-Big Ten and All-NCAA Tournament honors, won Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year and helped the Wolverines capture a national title. Not too shabby. He averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.4 dimes and a conference-leading 2.6 swats while shooting 66.8% from the floor and 56.4% from the charity stripe.
changed: Mara was selected No. 12 by the Thunder in the 2026 NBA Draft.
outlook: Chet Holmgren is on a long-term deal, and Isaiah Hartenstein re-signed with OKC in the offseason, so Mara will likely open his rookie campaign off the bench. He’s got the size and defensive skills to make an impact at the next level, so he could carve out meaningful minutes relatively quickly, especially if one of Holmgren or Hartenstein are forced to miss time. Mara is worth a look in deeper redraft leagues, and he’s a must-roster guy in dynasty formats.
